News.title: Customs officers left shocked as crocodile head discovered in suitcase
News.content:
Add us as a preferred source

CROC SHOCK Customs officers left shocked as crocodile head discovered in suitcase

STUNNED customs officers have discovered a whole crocodile head in a passengers suitcase.

An Italian man could face jail time after officials came across the dead reptiles head within his bag at Sandro Pertini airport in Italy.



The brazen passenger who had travelled from Miami through Istanbul is now the subject of a police probe.

The reptile’s head had been wrapped in brown paper packaging in an effort to conceal it from security checks and customs, the Turin unit of Italy’s financial police squad said in a statement.



It was swiftly seized by border authorities and the passenger, who was reportedly returning from a holiday, placed under investigation on allegations of smuggling a specimen belonging to a protected species.

If convicted, the croc smuggler could face a fine of between $23,200 and $232,000 or a six-month to one-year stint in prison.



Crocodiles are protected under the Washington Convention, a 1973 global agreement that restricts international trade to save endangered plants and animals.

Italy is a major transit hub for the illegal trade of exotic animals.

In a 2026 report, the Italian branch of the WWF said animals including “tortoises, ornamental birds, tropical reptiles and even small primates are illegally traded via online channels and cross-border exchanges”.

Exotic animal smuggling through airports is a massive international problem driven by global criminal networks.



In May three baby monkeys were found in the underwear of a Colombian couple as they tried to flee an airport.

One of to monkeys tragically suffocated in the ordeal.

A routine police check led to the harrowing discovery with the three primates strapped to the private parts of the pair of smugglers at the Rafael Núñez International Airport, Columbia.

The woman, 27, and the man, 26, both natives of La Jagua de Ibirico, had devised the twisted plan to evade immigration controls and were arrested.

Similarly, n February shocked airport staff found live monkeys and turtles in one audacious passengers luggage.



Officers pulled aside the man when they noticed suspicious outlines in his luggage.

They found 15 live animals, including 13 live big-headed and freshwater turtles, one langur and one gibbon.

He was arrested as police seized the protected animals, before handing them over to the Wildlife Conservation Office and the Fisheries Inspection Office.

News.title: David Lammy urged to stand as Labour’s candidate for London Mayor after being sacked as deputy PM
News.content:
DAVID Lammy is being urged to be Labour’s candidate for London Mayor after he was sacked as deputy PM.

Labour insiders said they have launched a campaign to “woo” the former Foreign Secretary to take a tilt at City Hall.



It comes amid a growing expectation that Labour London Mayor Sadiq Khan will not stand for a fourth term in 2028.

The race for London City Hall is already heating up.



Tory former Cabinet minister James Cleverly has announced he wants to be the Tory candidate.

Laila Cunningham is running for Reform UK.



A senior Labour Party figure said: “There is a concerted campaign to woo David Lammy to run.

“He would stand a real chance of winning.

“Currently the main person pushing herself is Dawn Butler – but she wouldn’t stand a chance.”

Mr Lammy was Sir Keir Starmer’s deputy PM.



“But he was sacked from the Cabinet when Andy Burnham became Prime Minister.

News.title: Massive fire rips through historic mill used for filming Peaky Blinders and Downton Abbey
News.content:
A HUGE inferno has ripped through a historic mill used for filming scenes in Peaky Blinders and Downton Abbey.

Plumes of smoke could be seen for miles after the blaze erupted at the building in Keighley, West Yorkshire, this evening.



Footage shows flames licking the roof of Dalton Mills as an orange glow illuminates the night sky.

Dozens of firefighters have been scrambled to the fire, which is believed to have erupted at around 8pm.



Residents are being evacuated as the blaze continues to ravage the Grade II-listed former textile mill.

West Yorkshire Fire and Rescue (WYFR) confirmed 12 fire engines are battling the fire.

One eyewitness described seeing swathes of smoke as they drove along the nearby A650.

They told the Telegraph and Argus: “I was driving down the A650 and I could just see all this smoke.



“I pulled over to have a look and I couldn’t believe the size of the fire.

“It’s unbelievable.”

The mill – which appeared in huge shows such as Peaky Blinders and Downton Abbey – was constructed in 1869.

It has suffered a string of major fires over the years, the first erupting in 2011.

Another blaze broke out in March 2022, when more than 100 firefighters and 20 fire engines tackled the inferno.



Another fire devasted the mill in July 2025, with 12 fire engines sent to the scene.

WYFR said: “Due to the severity of the incident and the potential risk to residents… a number of nearby residents are now being evacuated.

“Local Authority Emergency Planning officers are on scene and are providing support and guidance to those affected by the evacuation.

“If you are impacted, Local Authority Emergency Planning teams will communicate directly with you and provide further information and advice.

“We would like to thank residents for their cooperation and patience while our crews continue to tackle this incident.”

News.title: Bombshell plans to ABOLISH hated inheritance tax drawn up by Kemi Badenoch to take fight to ‘weak on economy’ Labour
News.content:
KEMI Badenoch plans to abolish inheritance tax if the Tories win the next general election.

The Conservative leader is hoping to announce the plan in her big party conference speech next month, a source told The Sun on Sunday.



Mrs Badenoch has criticised Andy Burnham as a tax-and-spend PM — as the economy shapes up to be a key battleground at the next election.

A Tory source said: “Kemi’s team think Labour are weak on the economy and plan to go hard on tax ahead of the election.



“Last year she said the Tories will abolish stamp duty on homes.

“This year they are looking to see if they can scrap inheritance tax if they can make the sums add up. It’s all about inspiration.”

Inheritance tax of 40 per cent has to be paid on everything above £325,000.

That threshold rises to £500,000 if a home is left to children or grandchildren.

The tax is hugely unpopular as it often means those who inherit a family home are forced to sell to cover the bill.

The Party conference, in Birmingham next month, is expected to be packed with policy announcements in case the PM calls an early election.



A Conservative spokesman said: “We have not decided our policy platform for the conference.

“Kemi has made no secret of her desire to cut taxes, singling out inheritance tax as one of those taxes she wants to cut in a speech last week.”

News.title: Fresh border misery as migrants set up camp near famous D-Day beach in new launch site to get to UK
News.content:
MIGRANTS have set up a camp close to the D-Day landmark Utah Beach from where a boat set off heading to Portsmouth last weekend – the longest known Channel crossing yet.

And The Sun on Sunday has identified the beach launch point – just several miles away from a camp where the migrants keep chickens and say they will stop at nothing to reach the UK.



At least four attempted crossings have been launched from the camp near Cherbourg, including last Sunday’s 140-person mega dinghy which landed 70 miles across the Channel at Portsmouth, sparking protests by hooded Patriots.

Céline Clement, 45, from nearby village Sainte-Marie-du-Mont, stumbled across identity papers, shoes, rucksacks and other objects while walking on an access road by Utah Beach the morning after the migrants set sail in the dead of night last Saturday.



She said: “There must have been about 10 pairs of shoes – there were water bottles and speakers for music too.

“The papers were like identity cards with names and surnames, but they also gave instructions on what to do in case of shipwreck.”



She also said that dinghies were already setting sail from the beach two years ago.

Céline added: “It’s not the first time – [migrants] have already come here to try to launch crossings.

“It’s not regular but the first time was about two years ago.

“This is the second crossing I’ve seen personally.



“The first time they tried to set sail but it didn’t work, and the boat was left in the water next to the D-Day museum on Utah Beach for a long time.”

A spokesperson for French NGO Itinérance told The Sun on Sunday that another attempted crossing from Utah Beach was foiled when an outboard motor with its serial number scratched out was found in Sainte-Marie-du-Monte in 2024.

She said: “This suggests that the smuggling routes are changing.



“But the passage west of Cotentin [west of Utah Beach] is even more dangerous for migrants.

“The increased police patrols [near Calais] are only making the route [to the UK] longer and even more dangerous.”

At the migrants camp Rafik Zaza, 25, from Afghanistan, said that the UK was still his ideal destination.

Our reporter found the camp is lined with dozens of tents, and has a shower, a makeshift gym and even a pen full of chickens providing eggs for residents.

It is also just a 45-minute bus or taxi drive from Utah Beach, making the journey by road much easier and closer than Calais, which is a four-hour drive away.



Rafik said that the camp is inhabited by dozens of Afghan males, all of whom are intent on seeking asylum in the UK.

He said: “I’ve not tried yet to go by boat to the UK, but others have.

“I have tried to board lorries going on the ferry to England from Cherbourg, but it’s harder now than it used to be.



“I want to go to the UK and everyone living here in the camp does as well.

“People die trying to get there but they still want to go.”

Cherbourg is home to a large community of Afghan asylum seekers – many are housed by the French state in the Octeville neighbourhood, known locally for its issues with crime.

Despite the crossings from this far-flung part of Normandy happening last weekend, senior officials in Border Force, the Home Office and Downing Street are reported to have said they do not believe this is the start of a new strategy by the criminal gangs.

One Border Force source said: “It’s too early to say for sure but there’s nothing to suggest that smugglers have changed their tactics.”



RECOMMENDED STORIES

But Rob McNeil, from Oxford University’s research project Migrant Observatory, told The Sun on Sunday that the aim of smugglers is to get dinghies into British waters, where they will be escorted to UK shores by the RNLI, regardless of the risk to passengers’ lives.

He pointed out that from Cherbourg, the distance to British waters is less than anywhere else on the French coast except from the Calais area.

News.title: Fury as MoD splashes almost £4k a time on chauffeur driven trips for staff – while Army CANCELS exercises to save £30m
News.content:
DEFENCE officials spent almost £4,000 a time on chauffeur-driven road trips for staff — while the Army cancels exercises to help save £30million.

New figures show the Ministry of Defence paid £3,850 each for 13 one-way journeys, including a 65-mile hop between two bases in the South East.



MoD travel records show its bill for taxis and chauffeur-driven cars was £1,932,244 from April 2024 to April 2025 — over £37,000 per week.

The bills, revealed in a freedom of information request, come after top brass were told to halt any large-scale training unless troops are about to deploy.



But Darwin Friend, of the TaxPayers’ Alliance, said: “Taxpayers will be astonished to see defence chiefs riding around in chauffeur-driven cars.

“With the defence budget already under enormous pressure and major training exercises being cancelled, shelling out millions of pounds on taxis and luxury travel is simply unacceptable.

“The MoD needs to crack down on waste and ensure scarce resources are focussed on the frontline.”

An MOD spokesperson said: “This Government is committed to securing value for money for taxpayers and cracking down on waste.

“These journeys involved multiple passengers and a significant amount of baggage.

“As a large organisation with remote sites across the UK and bases around the world, our staff sometimes need to travel to locations that are not always accessible by public transport.”

News.title: Moment bank robber throws chilli powder at staff before fleeing with handful of looted cash
News.content:
THIS is the moment a masked robber hurls chilli powder at bank staff before making off with over £3,000 in cash.

Footage shows a man in a white mask entering the bank before unleashing his spicy weapon on unsuspecting staff members.



Suraj Borker, 28, was arrested within 30 minutes of the incident at a State Bank of India branch in Maharashtra’s Nagpur district on Friday.

Cops allege Borker committed the robbery “out of greed for money“, The Indian Express reports.



The incident triggered widespread panic among the employees when Borker allegedly burst into the bank and assaulted them with chilli powder around 6 pm.

Footage captures Borker chasing down the employees to get a closer and more precise aim for his attacks.



Amid the chaos that ensued, Borker jumps the counter before allegedly grabbing a handful of cash – totalling around £3,503 – and fleeing.

A brave bank employee immediately chased down the accused along with officers who happened to be patrolling the area at the time.



The cops say Borker is currently unemployed, which may explain his wild actions.

It has also been reported that Borker was in a significant amount of debt which could further explain his decision to allegedly undertake the robbery.

Investigators are currently reviewing CCTV footage as part of their inquiry into the incident.



Police are now trying to find out whether anyone else was involved with him in the planning of the crime.

The entire sum of stolen money was recovered by police.

The footage has since gone viral on social media with one Facebook contributor saying: “At least it’s not a gun – way to spice up bank robberies”.

Earlier this year several armed thieves held 25 people hostage at an Italian bank.

The hostages were released around two hours into the terrifying ordeal after long negotiations between the cops and robbers.



The terrifying incident occurred at a Crédit Agricole branch in Naples in mid-April.

The armed robbers were believed to have escaped into the sewer system as authorities finally stormed the bank.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

In May a gang of armed robbers took two hostages in a terrifying bank raid in Germany where the suspects also vanished without a trace.

SWAT teams stormed the bank shortly after the reported heist before releasing the captured pair – but the perpetrators were nowhere to be seen.

News.title: Church of Scotland reverend suspended over church worker affair claims
News.content:
A MINISTER who quit to become a priest is being investigated over claims he had an affair with a former church worker.

Reverend Brian Casey, 55, is being probed by Kirk bosses over his switch to a breakaway Catholic church as well as allegations that he committed adultery.



The twice-divorced cleric, who was axed as minister of Glasgow’s Springburn Parish Church, denies cheating on his spouse, Sharon Logan, 56.

The minister-turned-priest has insisted they had split before he began a relationship with community worker Helen Carroll, 61.



Estranged wife Sharon said: “I am furious. I had suspicions about affairs going on for years. He just walked out of the manse.”

We told last year how the cleric had left his manse in Springburn, Glasgow, to join the Old Catholic Apostolic Church — and was calling himself Father Casey.

But in a blast at the Church of Scotland investigation into infidelity claims, he hit out: “They have said it’s an extra-marital affair with, amongst others, Helen Carroll. All of which is c**p.

“I’m suing the church for that accusation. I’ve spent £40,000 on a lawyer.

“I moved out of the manse in April 2025 and we got together the following month. We started to see each other as friends and it turned into something more.

“Don’t think we are having rampant sex everywhere we go because that’s not true. We still see each other two or three times a week.



“There’s no physical relationship at the moment.”

Rev Casey said he “won’t be engaging with the disciplinary process”.

He continued: “My relationship with my wife broke up in 2021. Church law is that I’m not allowed to leave the manse.



“So I slept on the couch for the last four years of our marriage.”

Helen helped Rev Casey — who once dressed up as Captain Kirk to lead the funeral of a Star Trek superfan and even gave a Vulcan salute — set up the St Jude’s Community in the city last year.

Months earlier, he was supported by members of his Springburn congregation in a fight to keep his job as minister amid claims he was being forced out as part of a restructuring drive.

Despite his claims that their marriage ended in 2021, his wife Sharon wrote an article backing her husband that was posted to Facebook in March last year.

She said it was “heartbreaking to watch the man you love” struggling to sleep due to “stress, pressure and uncertainty”.



Ms Carroll, who runs a community hub, said she was employed by the Church of Scotland after working with Rev Casey during the pandemic, but left in 2024.

She said the couple then became involved in a wellbeing cafe in early 2025.

She told The Scottish Sun on Sunday: “I started seeing him in March, April last year. It sticks out like a sore thumb that as soon as he moves out of the manse, we start having a relationship.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

“It’s not true that I broke up his marriage.”

A Church spokesman said Rev Casey is “currently under administrative suspension pending the conclusion of disciplinary proceedings”.

News.title: Will the Thirlwall report change the debate about Lucy Letby?
News.content:
The quick take is this. The report won't change the narrative about Letby's guilt or innocence because it didn't examine that subject at all. That wasn't its remit.

Lady Justice Thirlwall said she had "approached the inquiry on the basis that Lucy Letby is guilty of the crimes of which she has been convicted".

She emphasised that it was not her role "to set about reviewing the convictions", telling the inquiry: "The Court of Appeal has done that, with a very clear result."

But there is also a longer, more complex answer.

Whatever the report's conclusions, Letby's convictions will stand. However, the inquiry hasn't operated in a vacuum. There are other parts of the legal system which will have an eye on its findings.

And the chairwoman of the Criminal Cases Review Commission (CCRC) - the only organisation with the power to send Letby's case back to the Court of Appeal - has told the BBC the CCRC will be paying close attention to Thirlwall.

Dame Vera Baird said: "We will be looking at the report with interest to assess whether it has any bearing on our review of the case."

The CCRC has given no indication of when it will make its decision.

But while questions over Letby's convictions weren't within the scope of the Thirlwall Inquiry, it didn't stop the subject making itself felt within the hearing room.

Just as the inquiry was wrapping up, the hospital's former executives applied for it to be delayed until the CCRC has made its decision.

Letters pushing for a delay were also written to the inquiry by Letby's lawyers and Sir David Davis, an MP who has campaigned on her behalf.

Sir David argued that an inquiry "predicated on the presumption that Lucy Letby's conviction is safe, when there is now a wealth of authoritative voices questioning that conviction, will only undermine the conclusions arrived at by your inquiry and potentially lead to more babies dying unnecessarily".

Lady Justice Thirlwall refused the requests to pause the inquiry. She said that she was not scrutinising Letby's actions, but those of the officials and managers who were responsible for responding to the crisis.

News.title: Student loan terms to be made clearer in England
News.content:
University applicants in England will be given clearer information about student loans before they take them out, the government has said.

Ministers said they would spell out that governments can change repayment rules and that different career choices can affect how much borrowers repay.

They agreed to some but not all of the recommendations made by MPs after an inquiry into student loans, and did not say whether they would reverse a freeze to the repayment threshold for some graduates.

The inquiry found the way loans had been presented to teenagers amounted to mis-selling, after the BBC revealed the Department for Education (DfE) had compared repayments to Â£30-a-month phone contracts.

The recent debate has centred around Plan 2 loans, which were issued in England between September 2012 and July 2023, and are still issued in Wales.

The interest rate on those loans is the Retail Prices Index (RPI) measure of inflation plus up to 3% depending on earnings, and borrowers repay at a rate of 9% of everything they earn over a repayment threshold, which is meant to rise with inflation every year. The loans are written off after 30 years.

Campaigners want a lower interest rate, a lower repayment rate and for the government to reverse a decision last year to freeze the threshold at Â£29,385 for three years in England.

Freezing that threshold means graduates start repaying their loans sooner and, once they do, they pay more than they would have done if it had risen with inflation.

MPs on the Treasury Committee called for a U-turn on that decision as part of a series of recommendations after an inquiry this summer.

The Treasury and the DfE did not say whether ministers would unfreeze the threshold in their response, but said: "We keep all aspects of the student finance system under review."

News.title: Rybakina wins US Open to inflict further pain on Sabalenka
News.content:
Elena Rybakina demonstrated why she is the best women's player in the world by beating two-time defending champion Aryna Sabalenka to win her first US Open title.

Kazakhstan's Rybakina already knew she would be the new world number one after Saturday's final regardless of the result, and she celebrated with a 6-4 5-7 6-2 victory over the player she will replace.

Rybakina was the more composed of the two throughout as she claimed the third Grand Slam title of her career, having triumphed at Wimbledon in 2022 and the Australian Open earlier this year.

Sabalenka hoped to soften the blow of losing the top ranking by winning a third consecutive US Open title - but looked fraught in a tense performance.

Rybakina and Sabalenka have developed a strong rivalry built not only on their outstanding talent but their contrasting personalities.

And Rybakina's ice-cool composure - the direct opposite of the Belarusian's combustible nature - was a key difference as she took control at Flushing Meadows.

Rybakina stayed calm in an opening set where her first serve let her down and, despite her biggest weapon not firing on all cylinders, was able to execute a devastating returning game which left Sabalenka frustrated.

Sabalenka's groundstrokes improved as Rybakina's level dropped slightly in a tighter second set, taking her third opportunity to force a decider when she swarmed over Rybakina's second serve in the 12th game.

But the loose shots from Sabalenka reappeared in the third set - as did the negativity.

Rybakina's deep returning pinned Sabalenka to the baseline as she broke for a 2-1 lead, which allowed the incoming world number one to grow in stature.

There was a sign of nerves when Rybakina produced a double fault on her first championship point, but she reset admirably to hammer down an ace and underline her status as the best player in the world.

News.title: Reform receives second £36m donation in two days as crypto investor matches record
News.content:
Harborne has already donated millions to Reform and Farage, who is currently under investigation by the parliamentary standards commissioner over whether he should have declared a Â£5m cash gift from Harborne ahead of the 2024 election.

Farage has argued that he was under no obligation to register the "purely private" gift, as it was unrelated to his parliamentary or political activities.

The party is also facing scrutiny after a broadcast by Channel 4 News last week showed two senior Reform aides apparently suggesting a way around electoral law to secure foreign party donations.

The Metropolitan Police has said it is investigating, while the party denies any wrongdoing.

The force is also looking into donations given to the party by Fiona Cottrell, mother of longstanding Farage ally George Cottrell, as well as a company controlled by Tice.

Harborne wrote on Saturday that he had "already accumulated enough wealth for the rest of my life", while Reform was a "start-up party" that lacked "the benefit of hundreds of years of patronage".

"A start-up party needs more money than can be provided by membership fees alone, to build and sustain itself and be ready for government," he said.

Harborne and Delo's donations mark the largest sums received by a UK political party since they had to begin declaring them in 2001.

Delo, who also announced his donation in a Telegraph op-ed, said he was giving the money away because he wanted a "fair fight and a level playing field". He said in April he was moving back to Britain from Hong Kong.

Addressing the recent scrutiny of Reform's finances, he said: "My conclusion from Reform's recent troubles is that they should spend less time trying to raise funds to compete on equal terms and more time preparing for government."

Last year, he was given an unconditional pardon by US President Donald Trump over a breach of anti-money laundering laws at his crypto trading platform, BitMEX, to which he had pleaded guilty in 2022.

There are currently no restrictions on the amount of money UK-based donors can give to political parties.

However, the Labour government has introduced a Â£100,000 cap on donations from British citizens living overseas, and plans to introduce a similar one for those who have recently returned to the UK.

There were nine donations of Â£1m or more to political parties in 2025. The largest was Â£9m given to Reform UK by Harborne.

Labour had five donations of Â£1m or more - totalling nearly Â£10m - and the Conservatives had three of Â£1m each.

Labour said Reform and Farage still had "serious questions" to answer about their finances.

Party chairwoman Bridget Phillipson said Reform were "drowning" in "sleaze and scandal".

She added: "It's time Farage and Reform came clean with the public, fully co-operated with the ongoing police investigations and prove they're not just in it for themselves."

Rachel Millward, deputy leader of the Green Party, told BBC News it wanted a cap on donations from individuals of Â£500,000.

She said the donations to Reform were "absolutely staggering amounts", adding: "What I am very frustrated about is the influence of extreme wealth and the super rich. What I want to see is people in politics representing the needs of their communities and ordinary people."

Liberal Democrat Cabinet Office spokeswoman Lisa Smart called for the government to introduce emergency legislation to cap donations.

She said: "These are eye-watering amounts of money. This is real emergency for our democracy. It presents a very clear and present threat."

Labour MP Stella Creasy and other backbenchers had proposed an amendment to the Government's Representation of the People Bill that would stop donors giving parties over Â£100,000 a year.

But the amendment was never debated in the Commons after the government said it would set up a task force to investigate the issue. The bill will be debated in the House of Lords on Monday.

Duncan Hames, Director of Policy and Programmes at campaigning charity Transparency International UK, said: "This is a watershed moment, with two billionaires pledging Â£72m to one political party in less than 48 hours.

"This situation is now completely out of control, and makes an irrefutable case for government to bring forward an annual cap on political donations, and fast."

News.title: Diljit Dosanjh makes history under the famous Wembley arch
News.content:
On Saturday night, under the world-famous Wembley arch, five words rang out: "Punjabi Aa Gaye Wembley Oye!"

Indian megastar Diljit Dosanjh famously starts all his concerts by announcing that "the Punjabis have arrived".

But this time, it was a play on the usual catchphrase.

Dosanjh is the first ever Punjabi singer to headline Wembley Stadium, the music venue has said.

Addressing his fans, he reflected on the significance of the occasion. "This moment will go down in the history books," he said.

And as Bhangra beats blared out, fans erupted with cheers while Dosanjh launched into his biggest hits, from G.O.A.T. to Lover.

Over two decades, Dosanjh has built a huge global fanbase, topping charts and singing with the likes of Ed Sheeran.

He has even busted Bhangra moves with Jimmy Fallon, external, with the US talk show host labelling him "the biggest Punjabi artist on the planet".

His landmark concert at Wembley further cements his status as a global star.

Ahead of the show, the singer spoke exclusively to the BBC backstage, describing the moment as "a dream" for him.

News.title: Critics celebrate Céline Dion's 'high-stakes' comeback show in Paris
News.content:
Iconic Canadian pop singer CÃ©line Dion has kicked off her long-awaited comeback show in Paris on Saturday, after a six-year hiatus due to health issues.

The 58-year-old superstar was diagnosed with a rare neurological disorder called stiff person syndrome in 2022, which forced her to pull back from touring.

Dion, one of the best-selling musical artists of all time, has not performed a full show since a 2020 concert in New Jersey - the last before the Covid pandemic cut her tour short. In 2024, she performed just one song at the Paris Olympics closing ceremony.

Saturday marked the first of Dion's 26-show residency at the Paris La DÃ©fense Arena, Europe's largest covered concert arena.

"I made a promise," she told the Paris audience of about 30,000 people in her emotional return.

"I made a promise to come back, to be back on stage. And here I am. Singing for you, and singing for me," she said.

"I am everything I am because you loved me," she told the crowd.

She also broke down in tears after finishing a song, telling the audience: "I had promised myself not to cry."

"But I'm so happy to see you all. I missed you."

They weren't the only tears of the night, as the star appeared to be overcome with emotion several times.

Dion will be performing in Paris throughout September and October and into the New Year.

News.title: Some dentists say more young people are grinding their teeth - are you one of them?
News.content:
Ella can't remember when she first started grinding her teeth at night, but she can vividly recall the excruciating jaw ache, the headaches, and being told her molars were disappearing.

"I was in so much pain," Ella says. "My face was changing shape and my teeth were at risk of breaking - I knew I had to do something about it."

The 31-year-old has bruxism, a condition which can cause regular and often intense teeth grinding, but says the treatment she's recently had has "without a doubt" changed her life.

Bruxism affects millions like Ella across the UK, external. Some studies suggest nearly one in four people experience the condition, although many may be unaware until symptoms appear.

According to the British Dental Association there is some anecdotal evidence that bruxism is becoming more common, but no specific figures. However, some dentists have told the BBC they are worried about the increasing number of young people they're seeing with dental problems caused by incessant gnashing.

"It is definitely on the rise," Dr Aditi Desai, president of the British Society of Dental Sleep Medicine (BSDSM), says. "And it's no surprise given that life itself nowadays can be so stressful."

News.title: Drag Race co-creator fears for queer representation after BBC drops show
News.content:
The co-creator of Drag Race has said there is a "crisis of representation" on TV, following the BBC's decision to axe the UK edition of the show.

Speaking exclusively to BBC News, Fenton Bailey said he did not believe there was a "hidden agenda" behind the decision, but feared "vulnerable communities are going to be even more vulnerable".

The move led viewers to raise concerns about the corporation's on-screen representation, after it also cancelled two LGBTQ+ dating shows.

A spokesperson for the BBC said the decision was down to "significant financial pressures", as it attempts to make Â£500m of savings.

Other shows being cancelled include Celebrity Mastermind, Blankety Blank and Live at the Apollo, and more than 500 job losses have also been announced.

World of Wonder (WOW) announced future series of Drag Race UK, including a new All Stars version, will be broadcast exclusively on the company's own streamer, WOW Presents Plus.

BBC News spoke to Bailey, screenwriters, TV critics and former Drag Race contestants about the move and what it means for on-screen representation.

News.title: Burnham and Badenoch revive red versus blue politics as Reform land 'gobsmacking' donations
News.content:
Look closely at the posters, placards and online posts. Your eyes aren't deceiving you if Labour's red seems a little deeper and the Conservatives' blue a little truer.

Politics seems to have found a new rhythm, one that feels a little familiar, despite Reform's jaw-dropping new donations putting it back in the headlines today.

For the avoidance of doubt, the scale of that initial Â£36m gift to Nigel Farage's party alone is like something from a different political universe.

"It's a gobsmacking sum," a senior figure involved in running successive election campaigns for one of the big parties tells me.

That was even before another Reform donor pledged to match that astonishing sum with another Â£36m, saying the first donation had provoked his "competitive spirit".

But one cabinet minister is enjoying what they see as a newly obvious difference between Labour and the Tories. "It's clarifying," they say, a clear gap between Labour and the Tories' "sense of purpose and values".

A member of Conservative leader Kemi Badenoch's top team tells me, "normal jogging is reasserting itself", hopeful they're at the start of a more straightforward, routine moment in politics after years of craziness, with smaller parties vying to shove the traditional tribes out of the way.

The standout moment was at the despatch box this week when Prime Minister Andy Burnham declared that national security couldn't come at the expense of social security - a phrase immediately seized on by the Tories, interpreting it as the PM saying he'd never cut welfare spending to pay for defence.

News.title: Three arrests at rival protests in Portsmouth
News.content:
The new powers came into effect at 10:00 BST. Participants on both sides were not seen to be wearing any face coverings when the marches started.

The city centre protests follow disorder on 6 September, when police attended Eastney Marina as hundreds of demonstrators blocked roads in an attempt to stop coaches carrying 120 migrants, who had crossed the Channel in a dinghy, from leaving the city.

On Saturday, up to 500 anti-migrant protesters held Union and St George flags while some wearing Portsmouth Patriot branded clothing gathered outside All Saints Church on Commercial Road shortly before midday on Saturday.

The crowd chanted "stop the boats" as they marched to Guildhall Square.

About 300 people joined the counter-protest.

Both sets of demonstrators were kept apart by police when they arrived at the square.

Speaking before the march, Simon Magorian, of Stand up to Racism Portsmouth, described the demonstrations in Eastney as a "horrible spectacle".

He said: "Portsmouth is actually a good functioning multi-cultural city.

"We are now organising to have the broadest possible opposition to what we see as a fascist street movement and we're not going to allow them to get a grip on Portsmouth or any other town - this is quite terrifying."

News.title: A united Ireland would be 'fantastic' says Trump during Irish visit
News.content:
The Good Friday Agreement says the secretary of state must hold a border poll if it appears likely that a majority of people in Northern Ireland would vote for Irish unification - and the circumstances of when that could happen is the subject of constant debate in Northern Ireland and the Republic.

Earlier this week, Martin said there needed to be more clarity on when a border poll can be called, while Burnham ruled out calling a referendum, describing a poll as "off the table".

Sinn FÃ©in leader Mary Lou McDonald said she acknowledged Trumps comments on a united Ireland and said the onus is on the Taoiseach to begin planning.

Democratic Unionist Party (DUP) leader Gavin Robinson said Trump "knows better than most that elections matter".

"Northern Ireland's constitutional future will be decided by the people of Northern Ireland, not by commentary in London, Dublin or Washington," he said.

Former DUP MP Ian Paisley and close friend of the Trump family said: "everyone is allowed a personal opinion even when it's wrong".

Welcoming his comments, the leader of the Social Democratic and Labour Party (SDLP) Claire Hanna said there was something "fairly extraordinary" about Trump standing in Dublin and talking openly about Irish unity.

"When even Donald Trump has clocked that Irish unity is no longer some distant or theoretical prospect, it tells you something about just how far this conversation has shifted."

The Ulster Unionist Party (UUP) leader Jon Burrows said while America is an "important ally," Northern Ireland's future will be decided by its people".

The Traditional Unionist Voice (TUV) leader Jim Allister said Trump "is not the first US President to meddle in the affairs which don't concern him".

Ireland's Foreign Minister Helen McEntee said: "Something to this magnitude can only happen where there's consent from the Irish people.

"It's something that that we have to work on and we have to work towards."

Later, while attending an event at the US Ambassador to Ireland's residence, Trump said there is "no good answer" to a question about a united Ireland.

Recalling the moment, he said: "Oh that's a nice question, I have a nice answer, I think, we'll read about it tomorrow."

News.title: 'Skimpflation' warning as tinned mackerel alternative hits more supermarket shelves
News.content:
A growing trend of supermarkets selling a cheaper, less nutritious alternative to tinned mackerel is an example of "skimpflation", a consumer group has said.

Princes - which supplies major supermarkets - has substituted jack mackerel, an entirely different species, for mackerel, with similar tins also being sold by Lidl.

The switch has been spurred by dwindling stocks of Atlantic mackerel after years of overfishing, with its Chilean counterpart more sustainable and a third of the cost.

"It's a real concern when manufacturers quietly downgrade everyday staples like these as shoppers can end up paying the same price for a product that delivers significantly less nutritional quality," Sue Davies, head of food policy at Which?, said.

Jack mackerel contains about half as much omega-3 and around a third as much vitamin B12 as traditional mackerel.

The shift has prompted complaints from some consumers over differences in taste and texture, as well as concerns about how clearly the replacement fish is being labelled.

Princes announced last October, external that it was changing all of its tinned mackerel products to jack mackerel, saying the species meets the Marine Stewardship Council's sustainability standards.

The firm said its jack mackerel products were "clearly identified" and had been introduced following extensive product and consumer testing, describing it as having a "milder flavour and meatier texture".

Lidl is selling jack mackerel under its house brand. Lidl GB said it was "committed to sourcing fish and seafood from responsibly managed fisheries".

Davies from Which? said: "While manufacturers face genuine supply chain pressures and sustainability challenges, they have a responsibility to shoppers to be completely upfront when they change a product's recipe."

She added: "Skimpflation - quietly changing ingredients to cut costs - has become increasingly common, but it can feel particularly sneaky as shoppers may not realise a product has changed until they get it home and eat it."

News.title: Oscar-winning film producer Jeremy Thomas dies aged 77
News.content:
Oscar-winning producer Jeremy Thomas, whose films included The Last Emperor and Sexy Beast, has died aged 77.

The British filmmaker "passed away peacefully" surrounded by family and loved ones at his home in Oxfordshire on Friday, his publicist said in a statement.

Thomas built an international reputation over a career spanning five decades, working with directors including David Cronenberg, Nagisa Oshima, Julien Temple and Nicolas Roeg and backing independent films alongside mainstream successes.

His best known film, Bernardo Bertolucci's The Last Emperor, won nine Academy Awards, including best picture, and earned Thomas an Oscar as producer in 1988.

The critically-acclaimed biographical drama about the final monarch of China's Qing dynasty starred Joan Chen, Peter O'Toole and Vivian Wu.

Thomas repeatedly collaborated with Bertolucci, also producing The Sheltering Sky, Little Buddha, Stealing Beauty and The Dreamers.

He worked with several British directors at the start of their careers including Ben Wheatley, Jonathan Glazer, Stephen Frears and David Mackenzie.

Thomas's other credits included Oshima's Merry Christmas, Mr Lawrence - starring David Bowie - Cronenberg's A Dangerous Method, Roeg's Bad Timing and Eureka, and Matteo Garrone's Pinocchio.

He also produced Fast Food Nation, The Great Rock 'n' Roll Swindle, The Hit and adaptations of the JG Ballard books Crash and High-Rise.

After beginning as a film editor, London-based Thomas landed his first production role on the 1976 Australian film Mad Dog Morgan.

A former chairman of the British Film Institute, he won a Bafta for outstanding British contribution to cinema in 1990. Thomas received the European Film Academy's award for outstanding European achievement in world cinema in 2006 and was made a CBE in the New Year Honours in 2009.

Thomas's latest collaboration with Japanese director Takashi Miike, Bad Lieutenant:Tokyo, is due to premiere at the Toronto Film Festival on Monday.

News.title: Elderly woman found dead named by police
News.content:
An elderly woman whose death sparked a murder investigation has been named by police.

Thames Valley Police (TVP) said Jill Gant, aged 88, was found dead at an address on Appleford Drive in Abingdon, Oxfordshire at about 14:20 BST on Thursday afternoon.

Her family are being supported by specially trained officers.

A 36-year-old man from Abingdon who was arrested on suspicion of murder remains in police custody.

News.title: Battle to save the tiny, gooey snail only found in one lake in the UK
News.content:
A tiny snail found in only one lake in the UK has been dubbed as precious as an Egyptian artefact as conservationists bid to save it.

Several British zoos are setting up so-called ark populations of the glutinous snail, one of Europe's rarest species, using creatures bred in a back garden in Ceredigion.

"Beguiled by their cuteness," conservationist Ian Hughes has made it his "life-defining" mission to protect the threatened mollusc, which was once widespread in UK waters.

"There was a point where we'd got more snails in our garden than have ever been seen in the wild," he said.

News.title: Six people rescued after yacht gets tangled in fish farm
News.content:
Six people have been rescued after a 46ft yacht got into difficulty off the coast of Northern Ireland.

Red Bay Royal National Lifeboat Institution (RNLI) spent seven hours at sea in the early hours of Saturday morning off Cushendall, County Antrim.

Belfast Coastguard received a distress call from the boat, which had been travelling from Oban in Scotland to Portugal.

The yacht lost all power and steering after making contact with a fish farm in Red Bay, in 60 knots of wind, causing it to become trapped.

A lifeboat was launched at 03:22 BST, with an inshore lifeboat also launched.

In a statement Red Bay RNLI described the weather conditions as "difficult" due to "Force 9 gusting winds, driving rain and the darkness of night".

The RNLI crew observed that those on the yacht were safe and, given the difficult weather and sea conditions, the decision was made "for the sailors to remain onboard the yacht and for the lifeboat to standby until daylight broke" at 07:30.

At 09.30 the lifeboat crew "successfully freed the yacht from the fish farm and brought the sailors safely to Glenarm".

Those on the yacht stayed onboard the vessel while it was towed by the RNLI, who said there were no injuries.

The yacht is now receiving repairs.

Speaking following the call out, Paddy McLaughlin, Red Bay RNLI Coxswain said: "This was a challenging call out in difficult weather conditions, but we were delighted to bring the sailors to safety, and we would like to wish them well.

"We would also like to commend our colleagues in the Coastguard and thank our crew who responded quickly in the middle of the night, launched our lifeboats in darkness and made their way to the scene in what were gale force conditions, and for then spending seven hours at sea."

Conor Benn opens up on fatherhood, masculinity and Ryan Garcia

Tonight, Conor Benn fights for a world title for the first time, as he challenges Ryan Garcia for the WBC welterweight belt in Las Vegas.

A federal judge has ruled that a plan by the Trump administration to slash staffing at the federal agency tasked with responding to disasters by 50% was unlawful.

The opinion issued late Friday marked a victory for labor groups who had sued the agency. The labor organization had argued that plans by the Department of Homeland Security violated congressional protections that were designed to safeguard the independence of the Federal Emergency Management Agency.

The issue of the FEMA staffing was part of a much larger lawsuit filed by the American Federation of Government Employees and other labor groups, pushing back on efforts by the Trump administration to slash the federal workforce.

U.S. District Judge Susan Illston wrote in her opinion that top Homeland Security officials late last year directed FEMA's leadership to submit a staffing plan that included a 50% staffing cut even though the agency's own supervisors objected.

“Frankly, the FEMA staffing plan number appears as if pulled from thin air,” wrote Illston.

The Department of Homeland Security and FEMA did not immediately respond to requests for comment.

Illston wrote that it was clear that the government violated rules established after 2005's Hurricane Katrina that put decisions on staffing levels squarely in the hands of FEMA, not the Department of Homeland Security and that prevented DHS from “substantially” reducing the “functions” of FEMA.

Illston didn't order a specific remedy to carry out her opinion but directed the two sides to meet and decide on a course of relief.

Although FEMA has experienced terminations, the 50% staffing cuts ultimately were not carried out. In recent months, after top leadership changes at FEMA and the Department of Homeland Security, the agency has rehired some staffers who were let go.

FEMA was one of the agencies targeted in the federal government for staff reductions as part of a broad Trump administration plan to reduce the size of government. The embattled agency has been buffeted by mass staff departures, disruptions of grant programs, and delays of disaster aid.

In May, a Trump-appointed FEMA Review Council submitted a final report recommending sweeping changes to how the agency supports states, tribes and territories in disaster.

The final version backed away from the recommendation to cut the FEMA workforce by 50%, which was included in a December 2025 draft reviewed by The Associated Press.

The council instead recommended the agency conduct a “strategic review” to determine “appropriate staffing levels.”

In an August report, the Government Accountability Office said it found the departures of thousands of staff in 2025 resulted in a “loss of institutional knowledge and experienced personnel” and “exacerbated longstanding workforce challenges.”

More than 4,300 employees, or about 17% of FEMA’s workforce, separated from the agency in the 2025 budget year, with over 1,500 through voluntary reductions. The agency also made about 2,900 new hires.

The GAO recently recommended to Congress that it “consider requiring” FEMA to base “significant workforce decisions” on a more strategic planning process.

Without it, the GAO found, “FEMA cannot be assured that the agency is positioned to effectively meet its mission needs.”

News.content:
South Africa lifted the first Rugby's Greatest Rivalry trophy ( AP )

South Africa rugby sealed a 3-1 success in the inaugural Rugby’s Greatest Rivalry series with an entertaining 43-28 victory in Baltimore.

Having ensured that they could not be beaten with back-to-back wins on South African soil, the Springboks surged away to wrap up the tour outright with a strong win. Scrum half Morne van den Berg was to the fore with an all-round performance, while Kurt-Lee Arendse lit up the second half with a scintillating solo score to help put the game beyond doubt.

The world champions were deserved winners, on balance, having fought back from falling behind in a stunning defeat to the All Blacks at Ellis Park. New Zealand boss Dave Rennie could take heart, though, from the fact that his side were never blown away, staying in the fight right to the last with veteran Beauden Barrett scoring the last try of the night at M&T Bank Stadium. Can they rise to challenge the Springboks for World Cup glory next year?

Elena Rybakina proved herself to be the undisputed world number one after claiming her first US Open title.

The 27-year-old from Kazakhstan knew she would be top of the rankings from Monday, overtaking her opponent Aryna Sabalenka, whatever the outcome of Saturday’s final.

A defeat would have certainly taken the shine off that achievement, but instead she was crowned the new queen of Queens at Flushing Meadows after a 6-4 5-7 6-2 victory.

Two-time defending champion Sabalenka was looking to become only the third woman to achieve a New York ‘three-peat’ in the Open era, after Chris Evert and Serena Williams.

open image in gallery Elena Rybakina powered away from Aryna Sabalenka ( AP )

Instead she was left sat in her chair, furiously smashing her racket in to smithereens as Rybakina celebrated a third grand slam title.

“I honestly was coming here for the last 10 years and it was never successful, nothing close to that and it’s just incredible,” she said. “I’m falling in love with New York more and more. It’s amazing memories for me.”

Rybakina is an inscrutable presence on one side of the net compared to the unfiltered Sabalenka, who was clearly rattled early on and gave up the only break in the first set with a double-fault,

Yet at 5-4 on serve in the second, the top seed found one of her best shots of the tournament, a backhand at full stretch down the line to bring up two set points.

Rybakina survived that, but a bad miss at the worst time gave Sabalenka a third chance and she punished a second serve to level the match.

open image in gallery Aryna Sabalenka was left disappointed ( PA )

The momentum should have been with Sabalenka, but instead she had to ward off a break point at the start of the third before Rybakina held to love.

A stunning winning return, a Sabalenka miss and a hurled racket later, Rybakina had broken early in the third set, before another Belarussian howl of anguish as a volley flew past signalled a second, killer break for 5-2.

Serving for the title was not without its jeopardy with two double-faults – including one on championship point – but an ace clinched the crown as well as a winner’s cheque of $5.5m (£4.1m), a record pay-out at a grand slam.

A tearful Sabalenka, 28, said: “The last thing I want to do now is give a speech, but I’ll try my best.

open image in gallery Aryna Sabalenka released her frustration after defeat in New York ( AP )

“Obviously I’m disappointed but I want to congratulations Elena on an incredible year and an incredible result. Enjoy it.”

“I wish I could perform a little bit better, but I guess next year.”

Explaining her racket smashing at the end, she added: “It’s really tough to control your emotions when you lose in the final of the grand slam and when you were trying to go for ‘three-peat’.

“So I just wanted to let it go, because if I held it inside, right now or here or there on the court, I wouldn’t be able to say a word or I would just be not really nice.”

PA

News.title: Springboks look like World Cup champions elect… again
News.content:
In doing so, Erasmus while still relying on his veteran performers, managed to expose some of the next generation to invaluable white heat pressure, including Sacha Feinberg-Mngomezulu, Morne van den Berg and Cameron Hanekom, who all look to the manor born.

And the substance of the series victory is heightened by the fact it came against a regenerated and rejuvenated All Blacks side, who rediscovered their high-octane and relentless attacking identity under new coach Dave Rennie. At times the handling and precision of the All Blacks were so sumptuous that it felt like they might be in a position to level the series in Baltimore.

But the narrative of the previous two Tests continued. At key moments they were let down by their discipline and turnovers in attack to gift the Springboks’ transition ball, and their directness, backed by their power both in collisions and set piece enabled them to pick up points much more easily than their opponents.

At the end, the scoreboard ran away from the All Blacks, which was harsh on them. But one had wondered if they would be able to maintain their intensity at the end of the first half, when it took 32 phases for Will Jordan to score a try to cut the deficit to three points.

News.title: Emotions run high and Sabalenka smashes racket after Rybakina clinches US Open
News.content:
The polarities reversed in set two, as Sabalenka began to get her flamethrower of a forehand working. After almost 90 minutes of play, she finally chiselled out some break points – two in game 10, which she couldn’t convert, but then another in game 12 which set up the decider.

The huge contrast in personalities became all too evident in set three. Sabalenka appeared to be at war with herself, emoting and venting almost as if she were an actress projecting her feelings to the whole of this 24,000-seater stadium. As she faced the prospect of slipping a double-break down, she hunkered down on her haunches in despair.

Meanwhile, Rybakina could have been relaxing in a flotation tank for all the stress she showed. Admittedly, she did hit a couple of double-faults as she served out for victory, but she also came up with two aces and two forehand winners in the same game.

Sabalenka, meanwhile, allowed her racket to slip to the ground in frustration and barely managed a brief embrace at the net. She had earned a code violation in the first set for slamming a ball out of the stadium, and could easily have picked up a second – and thus a point penalty – after another ball that she batted away struck a cameraman, but chair umpire Greg Allensworth showed leniency.

Asked about tossing her racket, Sabalenka said: “It’s really tough to control your emotions when you lose in the final of the Grand Slam and when you were trying to go for three-peat. So I just wanted to let it go, because if I would hold it inside, right now or here or there on the court, I wouldn’t be able to say a word or I would just go not really nice over there.

“So I just wanted to let all of that aggression and disappointment go outside.”

The trophy was presented by 2006 champion Maria Sharapova – one of the few women who can look down on 6ft Rybakina, especially when wearing heels. The fans in Arthur Ashe Stadium had given at least 80 per cent of their support to Sabalenka, who won the previous two US Opens on this court, but they applauded warmly, knowing when they had seen a performance for the ages.

News.title: Former Geordie Guimaraes taunts Sunderland fans as Arsenal show mark of champions
News.content:
Hello and welcome to live, minute-by-minute coverage of Sunderland v Arsenal at the Stadium of Light. Sunderland are the latest team tasked with stopping Arsenal, who have begun their title defence in formidable style: they’ve won out of three, including a dominant comeback victory against Chelsea last weekend, and look well equipped to become the first Arsenal team to retain the title since the mid-1930s.

There’s a long way to go, and Arsenal fans will remember how blisteringly they started their last two title defences in 2002-03 and 2004-05, only to ultimately fall short. But right now, they could barely be in better shape. Their fine start to the season came with a Champions League win in Naples, achieved despite a delay to their flight from London.

“I love those challenges,” said Mikel Arteta. “I try to create them in pre-seasons so when they happen, we already experience them and we already know. So get to the stadium very late, change the routine and suddenly the players have to do something else.

“Because when it happens, and it can happen, you can miss the flight, the train can be delayed, there’s so much traffic and I don’t want the players, but not only the players, the staff as well, panicking. So when that happens, adapt to it.”

Arteta has tested his squad in a variety of ways. “[We have] delayed the meals, delayed the transport, taken a different route. We’ve done many things – made the dressing room hotter, more difficult, more challenging, less beds... because we’re going to have to adapt to different contexts.”

So far, they’re adapting very well to the context of being the reigning champions.

Kick off 8pm.

News.title: £329m spent and still no goals for sorry Tottenham
News.content:
Tottenham Hotspur have never before in the club’s history begun a league season without scoring a single goal in the first four games, although having done so after spending £329m on new players really does take some doing.

“Please score a goal!” was the homemade sign from two Spurs fans upon which the television cameras lingered at the end of the game, although the jaunty felt-tip design and glued-on team crest were rather upbeat compared to the gloom of the stadium. Spurs have tried to outrun their past but it just keeps catching up with them.

A team reimagined, a manager freshly launched and yet they are back in the same grip of anxiety that accompanied them on two consecutive 17th-place finishes in the last two seasons. By the end of this they might have been glad to escape with a single point against Everton, the one team in the Premier League who closed the window with a net transfer profit.

For Roberto De Zerbi, there was another passionate defence of his team afterwards. “The people, the fans already understand if I make excuses or not,” he said. “I came last season when the s--- was like this”, he gestured to a level somewhere around the midpoint of his forehead. “I have always been… not positive but realistic. I am sorry for the result that it’s not immediately the improvement. We played as a team. We didn’t score. We didn’t win [but] we played as a team.”

News.title: Xabi Alonso hits out at ‘soft’ Chelsea players
News.content:
Xabi Alonso accused his Chelsea players of being “soft” after they failed to keep a clean sheet for the 20th successive Premier League game.

Chelsea threw away an early lead to draw 2-2 with Hull City and have conceded two or more goals in each of their four Premier League games.

Alonso has tried different systems and different players in those games, but suggested Chelsea’s biggest problem is mental.

The club’s dreadful clean-sheet record pre-dates him and is the first time in 65 years Chelsea have gone 20 league games without keeping the opposition out.

Hull’s first goal from Mohamed Belloumi came after the ball had bounced over Jorrel Hato and Alonso said: “We need to be aware that from any situation, any team in the Premier League can hurt you. Today it was from a long ball, two bounces, the way it happened. You need to be very aware, very ready that the danger can come from any situation. If you are soft or if you are not prepared, you will get punished and we have been punished that way.”

Chelsea have shared 30 goals with their opponents in the club’s six games in all competitions so far this season.

News.title: Lando Norris on pole for Spanish GP but adds voice to critics of ‘Madring’
News.content:
Red Bull’s Max Verstappen predicted that overtaking would be “practically impossible” in the race. “[The Madring] has a tendency of maybe creating some big shunts in some places,” the Dutchman said. “It reminds me a little bit of Jeddah in a way – fast corners and the walls being very close.

“The only thing that’s already a bit disappointing is that many of the braking zones are angled. This means it’s practically impossible to attack a competitor because you’re braking and simultaneously turning right or left. And that’s the worst thing you can do if you want to create an overtaking opportunity.”

Norris agreed with Verstappen that it would be very difficult to overtake, although that is no bad thing for him provided he can hang on to the lead at the start.

The Briton, though, described the decision to build what is now the longest pit lane on the F1 calendar as a big disappointment.

“I think it has a lot of potential,” Norris said of the Madring. “Just certain things need to be improved. Like the pit lane, which is like six kilometres long. It’s the longest pit lane of the year and the biggest pit loss of the year [in terms of the time it will take to pit – an estimated 25 seconds]. So that just makes overtaking worse. Not overtaking, but it makes the desire to box and do different strategies worse.

“You know, if we’re going to build a new track and spend so much money in building a new track, this is probably one of the main factors, I would say, is you have a short pit lane so people can pit and you then create overtaking.”

Norris described his pole lap as “one of the best laps of his career” and his team principal Andrea Stella fully agreed, describing it as “a masterpiece”.

News.title: Bomb squad rescues rusty Red Roses
News.content:
Mia Venner, Sadia Kabeya, Lucy Packer and Claudia Moloney-MacDonald went over for further tries to add to player-of-the-match Abi Burton’s first-half score.

Moloney-MacDonald’s try wide out on the left was a show-stopper for the crowd of 9,251 in the North West and demonstrated that England have style to go with solidity. But it was the power game that did for Australia.

The Wallaroos scored tries of their own through Faliki Pohiva and Eva Karpani but spent the vast majority of the game manning the defensive barricades. They did so admirably for 40 minutes but when the dam wall blew it blew spectacularly.

They did not help themselves with sin-binnings in either half for Samantha Wood and Karpani, but over 80 minutes the odds will always be stacked in favour of the full-time side against the part-timers.

“The reality is that even at our best we’re probably not good enough. We will be,” said Tim Walsh, Rugby Australia’s director of women’s high performance. “We need an environment where they can concentrate on being full-time athletes. That’s the vision Rugby Australia have and that’s where we’re headed.”

The game was England’s first with the smaller ball being trialled in the women’s game by World Rugby and they only converted four of their eight tries, a statistic which may be seized upon by those who do not care for it. A rugby pitch is not a sterile laboratory though and the swirling, blustery conditions should be taken into account in any dissection of its value.

News.title: Jordan Cox looks a Joe Root clone as pair steer England home
News.content:
There is perhaps no batsman in Test history as accustomed as Joe Root to walking in with the scoreboard reading “not many for two” and his team in a tight spot.

That is where Root found himself once again soon after 11am on Saturday. His team were two for two, with both openers out for ducks, and the problems of the third evening bleeding into the fourth morning. A chaotic and patchwork Pakistan team suddenly believed Mohammad Abbas could inspire their defence of 130.

A familiar position for Root, sure, but not the young man at the other end, the rookie No 3 Jordan Cox. Together, they eased England out of a creeping crisis with such aplomb that the target was chased swiftly enough that the few thousand at Edgbaston were refunded 50 per cent of their ticket prices because so few overs were bowled. When Cox hit the winning run, a scrambled single into the off side, Root’s relief was palpable. His team had been tested, and he felt they would be “better for it”.

They had won his first series since returning to the captaincy 3-0, but not without a scare at the last. The scorecard will record this as a routine England eight-wicket win and, for the most part, it was. But England were rattled by Razaullah, a 21-year-old who spent the first two Tests of this series in Mardan, in the mountains of the Khyber Pakhtunkhwa region near Pakistan’s border with Afghanistan. Having bowled quickly, he wreaked havoc on the third evening with his 63-ball 81, taking England from the brink of an innings victory to an awkward chase.

Razaullah’s partner with the bat was Abbas, who provided England with an almighty fright on the fourth morning. First ball, Ben Duckett was caught behind. The ball was angled in, demanding that it was played, then nipped slightly away, taking the edge. Duckett’s trudge off was glacial, with his curious Test summer over. He has scored England’s only century of the season, but failed to make fifty otherwise. In this series, he has averaged just eight.

It came right when the Gunners were rocking. But those two moments of brilliance continued Arsenal’s 100 per cent start to their Premier League defence.

The result piles the pressure on rivals Manchester City – who trail by three points ahead of the derby at United.



One of the key reasons behind Arsenal’s rampant form has been their success at getting Marton Odegaard into more advanced positions.

Including the Community Shield, the Norwegian has scored four in six, after just one in their entire title-winning Prem campaign.

Sunderland had clearly done their homework. They were on him like wasps throughout the first half.

Sports.title: Former Prem ace Shane Duffy paid OnlyFans model to strip and dress like his ex Katie Price in kinky five hour video call
Sports.content:
FORMER Prem ace Shane Duffy paid an OnlyFans model to strip off in a video call — and asked her to change the colour of her undies.

Kelly Blake said the defender, who has dated Katie Price, paid £1,100 to keep her on the FaceTime chat for five hours.





Kelly — a lookalike for Katie when the glamour model was in her heyday — claimed Duffy, 34, who has played for Premier League clubs including Brighton, peeled off his clothes while lying on the sofa.

She said: “Shane asked me to slip out of my bra, which I agreed to.

“Then I had to change into a different blue bra, knickers and high heels, which was fun. He liked that colour.

“He kept saying, ‘You’ve got great t*ts’.

“I eventually ended the call because he wasn’t paying any more money. But it went on for a very long time.

“After the call, he messaged me the next day asking if I was OK and that was it.”

She revealed Republic of Ireland international Duffy made three payments into her bank account during the lust-fuelled call.

He sent her £300 at 3.44am, £200 at 4.14am, then £600 at 6.37am.





Kelly, 37, added that the centre back, a free agent after being released by Norwich City in June, also asked her to send him two raunchy videos.

She said he later told her: “I can’t stop thinking about it since. Is that bad?”

Kelly added: “He asked me to fly to Ireland and have a session with him.”

She has won an army of fans by posting sexy photos on social media.

Kelly had the five-hour call with 6ft 4in Duffy on August 25.

Their first interaction was earlier in the year when the footballer saw her saucy snaps and sent her a message saying: “Oh hello I see you! Don’t even know ya, but shall I take you on a date this week?”

Duffy, who has also played for Everton, Celtic and Blackburn Rovers, has had a turbulent love life.

In 2017 he was at the centre of a bust-up after a photo of him naked in a woman’s bed was posted online — and seen by his then missus.



A year later, it was revealed Duffy had started dating Katie.

An insider said at the time: “When their relationship was exposed, Shane immediately seemed to get cold feet and stopped seeing Katie. He wasn’t keen on the publicity and things went cold after that.”

Their trysts were revealed when Katie’s hard-to-miss pink Range Rover was seen outside Duffy’s home.

In 2023, the Sun On Sunday told how Duffy snogged a mystery woman on a night out while dressed as Dorothy from the Wizard of Oz.

Snaps of the clinch devastated his then missus.

Duffy helped Brighton win promotion to the Premier League in 2017 before eventually leaving for Fulham in 2023.

He told The Sun: “I’m aware of the comments that have surfaced online following the recent coverage involving Kelly and me.

“Some of what is being circulated relates to things I said online when I was considerably younger, while other claims are rumours, accusations or versions of events that I do not accept as accurate.



“I completely respect Kelly’s right to distance herself from me, particularly if she feels that continued association could expose her to criticism because of things being circulated about me.

“I don’t hold that against her in any way. For clarity, Kelly and I have only ever been friends; we were never in a relationship.”

Sports.title: Furious Arteta rages over 'unacceptable' Sunderland penalty call
Sports.content:
A furious Mikel Arteta described Sunderland's penalty in Arsenal's 2-0 win at the Stadium of Light as "unacceptable".

The home side were awarded a spot kick in the 54th minute when defender Ezri Konsa was adjudged to have held Sunderland's Dan Ballard by referee John Brooks.

"The referee's call of penalty to Sunderland for a holding offence by Konsa on Ballard was checked and confirmed by VAR," said a statement published by the Premier League Match Centre.

The statement continued by quoting the interaction between on-pitch referee Brooks and the VAR.

David Raya saved Enzo Le Fee's spot kick and Bruno Guimaraes scored Arsenal's opening goal just 121 seconds later but Arteta vented his anger at the decision despite the result.

"The first question we have to discuss is this," he said at the start of his press conference. "This is not acceptable at this level.

Elena Rybakina cemented her position as world No 1 by dethroning two-time US Open winner Aryna Sabalenka to seal her maiden title in New York.

Rybakina ​won ‌her ​first US Open, beating top seed ‌and defending champion ⁠Sabalenka ​6-4 ​5-7 ⁠6-2 on Arthur Ashe Stadium.

The 27-year-old had already been guaranteed to replace Sabalenka at No 1 in the rankings next week.

An ankle injury ‌had threatened to derail Rybakina's campaign even before the tournament started, but she shrugged off those ​concerns to add the US Open title to her Australian Open triumph this year and Wimbledon success in 2022.

Sports.title: Guimaraes haunts Sunderland as Arsenal continue winning start
Sports.content:
Bruno Guimaraes scored a stunning goal two minutes after David Raya had saved a penalty as Arsenal beat Sunderland 2-0 to move above Manchester City at the top of the Premier League.

The Black Cats had the chance to go in front when Ezri Konsa was penalised for holding Dan Ballard in the second half, a decision which enraged Arsenal manager Mikel Arteta, but Raya brilliantly tipped Enzo Le Fee's spot kick onto the post.

Just 121 seconds later, Guimaraes, whose every touch had been booed by the home fans due to his Newcastle connections, crashed a stunning strike in off the underside of the crossbar from outside the Sunderland box for his first Arsenal goal.

The victory, Arsenal's fourth in a row in the Premier League and sixth in all competitions, maintains their strong start to the campaign and puts the champions three points above Manchester City, who face Manchester United live on Sky Sports on Sunday.

For Sunderland, the defeat is made all the more painful by the identity of the player who opened the scoring, coming so soon after they appeared poised to strike first from the spot. They remain on four points, the latest side to be dispatched by Mikel Arteta's men.

Arteta rages at Sunderland penalty call

Arsenal manager Mikel Arteta to TNT Sports: "It's a huge win but it could have been something very different.

"I'm so upset. It's unacceptable (Sunderland's award of a penalty). This can change the course of a season, the championship, and it's not acceptable.

"I've seen it 10 times to make sure because I watched it live and I said it's not possible that it's going to be a penalty because it's a judo role, that's what it is. It cannot happen.

"It's not a penalty in any case, in any context, in any league."

Is Raya the world's best goalkeeper?

Sky Sports' Nick Wright:

Guimaraes didn't hesitate when asked after the game if he sees David Raya as the best goalkeeper in the world. "Definitely," he said.

The midfielder's sensational goal completed the two-minute turnaround but it was Raya who made it possible.

Arteta was adamant the spot kick should never have been awarded. But Raya's sole focus was to stop it from going in. Le Fee, who scored a penalty last weekend, struck it well. Raya, though, showed his athleticism, diving low to his left to make the save.

It was a brilliant piece of goalkeeping and there were plenty of other examples over the course of the 90 minutes at the Stadium of Light. Sunderland are about as physical as opponents come but he dominated his box, claiming crosses and exuding calm.

His save to deny Mukiele, following a fabulous centre by Granit Xhaka, when Arsenal were still only a goal up, was another crucial intervention. And he was straight back up on his feet to scramble away the follow-up. Raya is always alert to danger.

He had to settle for a place on the bench with Spain at the World Cup. But there can be little doubting his status as the Premier League's best, if not the world's, and his value to his team-mates and manager is abundantly clear.

He was Arsenal's difference-maker - and not for the first time.

Guimaraes: A beautiful moment for me

Arsenal's Bruno Guimaraes to TNT Sports: "It's unbelievable. I feel very good.

Image: Bruno Guimaraes celebrates his goal against Sunderland

"Everyone knows I had a difficult start with injuries in a short time but I'm glad to be back, to play.

"I scored a beautiful goal. It's a beautiful moment for me and my family and I'm very happy.

"A beautiful goal in a very good place. Everyone knows my past. I had an amazing history at Newcastle but now I'm trying to create a new history here and I've started in the right way."

Le Bris: Proud but disappointed

Sunderland head coach Regis Le Bris: "Proud and disappointed. These are the two words I have in my mind at the minute.

"Proud because we showed we were really close to achieving something really big against one of the best teams in Europe right now.

"Our second half was excellent. We got the momentum, created chances. A big save from Raya on the penalty. The league is relentless. We conceded the goal but we stayed in the game.

"We created other chances but didn't score and this is the difference today."

The Spaniard's words of wisdom helped his son reset after his sensational five-set win over defending champion Carlos Alcaraz in the quarter-final.

"I think you learn from your experiences," said 60-year-old former ATP pro Shelton. "He won Montreal, he went to Cincinnati and we said: 'this is going to be the toughest day you're going to have', playing in the first round in Cincinnati after winning a title.

"Very few people come from that and have another good tournament the next week, and he didn't, you know? He lost first round.

"I remember talking to Rafa a couple of days after that match. Rafa was, like, 'you know, you got to be able to get through that first one and have the day off and then be able to get your best tennis again the next week'.

"So it was a lesson for Ben that you've got to be able to bounce back when good things happen, just as you have to bounce back when adversity happens or tough things go on.

"So we talked about him beating Carlos and how important it's really going to be for him to understand that this one is going to be even tougher, you know, to bounce back after that, because a lot of people want to rest after they've had something good and want to celebrate it.

"What we say is don't celebrate until you separate. So you've got to win the next match. You've got to consolidate it. Then somewhere, hopefully next week, we can celebrate a little bit."

French Open champion Zverev was pushed to five sets in each of his opening two ​rounds, but has now won four straight matches without dropping a set to charge into his third consecutive major final ⁠and stand in Shelton's path.

"I enjoy these kind of atmospheres," said the German.

"I've said it before. I played a lot of French guys in France. I think the most hostile crowd, if you call it that, is when you are playing a French player in Paris Bercy back in the day.

"That was quite intense, and I always enjoyed those. I always enjoyed those kind of atmospheres.

"Of course, I played Australian guys in Australia. I played Arthur Fery in Wimbledon. The Wimbledon crowd is a bit different, though. There's no question about that.

"For me, a loud and energetic crowd is always great, as long as they're fair, as long as they don't interrupt in the middle of points. Other than that, I always enjoy these kind of atmospheres."
