Sports.title: West Ham secure first WSL win of season against London City Lionesses
Sports.content:
West Ham claimed their first Women's Super League win of the season with a 2-1 home victory over London City Lionesses.

Kelly Gago put the Hammers ahead after 21 minutes, racing onto Seraina Piubel's pass from near halfway before rounding City goalkeeper Elene Lete.

Viviane Asseyi scored a similar goal three minutes after the break after being released by Riko Ueki, running clear from 40 yards out before firing home.

Image: West Ham's Viviane Asseyi celebrates after scoring to make it 2-0

London City set up a frantic finish after Danielle van de Donk's clever back heel crept in at the near post 14 minutes from time.

But the Lionesses struggled to reproduce the fluency that had seen them overcome Manchester United on the opening weekend.

Guarino: We must show same spirit in every game

West Ham head coach Rita Guarino

"I'm very happy.

"I'm happy with the result, it's three important points at home in front of our supporters, but also for the performance in the way the team played today, and the way the team trained in the week.

"I'm very happy with the result and performance.

"I saw the spirit that I want to see every time, it's part of our identity. We can't forget that we have this kind of value and we need to show it in every single game.

Sports.title: Iraola bemoans Liverpool's lack of cutting edge and explains Barcola plan
Sports.content:
Liverpool manager Andoni Iraola bemoaned lack of creativity and cutting edge after his side were held to a 0-0 draw by Fulham at Anfield.

The result leaves Iraola unbeaten so far this term, but Liverpool have yet to win at home in the Premier League this season.

Liverpool struggled to create opportunities against a Fulham team that had lost their opening three games, with Iraola insisting afterwards that his side's shortcomings were evident.

"I think what was lacking, I think it was quite clear," Iraola said.

"I think it's the first game since I'm here, I think we've had problems to create chances, to score goals, to make the difference offensively.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player FREE TO WATCH: Highlights from Liverpool’s match against Fulham in the Premier League

"That's the main reason. We couldn't create as many chances as we wanted and we haven't scored a goal. And that's why we go just with one point."

Iraola: Players lacked freshness

Image: Fulham's Gonzalo Garcia and Liverpool's Ronald Araujo battle for the ball

The Reds lacked the energy they showed in their midweek Champions League win over Atletico Madrid, but Iraola refused to use fatigue as an excuse for his side's failure to pick up all three points.

"Our players were tired," he said.

"I think there is a lack of freshness, definitely. We cannot hide it.

"I think it's the worst turnaround in terms of 60-something hours between the games, after a very big game (against Atletico Madrid) the other day.

Image: Oscar Bobb is challenged by Milos Kerkez

"But this is going to happen more times, maybe with one more day, maybe. But sometimes it's going to happen the same way during the season. We have to adapt to these circumstances.

"It's this kind of game that you need to win, sometimes with a set play, sometimes with a shot from the edge, sometimes from a moment of brilliance from the offensive players and we haven't had that today.

"We've been clearly not as good offensively as we've been in other days."

Barcola makes full PL debut from left

Bradley Barcloa made his full Premier League debut in the game and was deployed from the left in a 4-2-3-1 formation, with Victor Munoz starting the game on the right.

Explaining his thinking, Iraola said: "I think I said it a lot of times. I think we have four wingers. Probably, before the season, everyone will say there are more left wingers than right wingers, because they play more there.

"I think all the wingers will play on the right and will play on the left. Depending on the match-up, depending on where we think they are going to be more dangerous, depending on the defensive demand, depending on what we feel, what we analyse, we position them in the right or in the left.

"But I think Bradley, I think everyone. The four of them already have played both sides and it's going to be a whole season like this because of the wingers, with a lot of times the same preferences."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Thierry Henry explained why Liverpool supporters should be excited by new signing Bradley Barcola after the France forward completed his move from Paris Saint-Germain in a deal worth up to £123m

Iraola added: "I think with Bradley now we are building also his physical condition, because he hasn't had any in pre-season and I think there is a good part where today he played, I think, a little bit more than three days ago against Atletico Madrid.

"He had a good chance in the second half, they blocked the shot but he arrived well.

"Probably, we know he has more, but now it's about giving him the minutes, keep building his confidence also and he's a player that is worthy of our support."

Sports.title: Guimarães and Saka fire Arsenal to win at Sunderland after Raya spot-kick save
Sports.content:
As the final whistle blew Bruno Guimarães wore a mischievous smile, Enzo Le Fée was a study in dejection and Arsenal’s immaculate start to the season remained unblemished.

Two minutes after David Raya had rather majestically saved Le Fée’s second-half penalty, Guimarães delighted his new north London public and plenty of old friends in Newcastle by sending a shot curving past Robin Roefs from the edge of the area.

Mikel Arteta’s champions were en route to another win in a campaign that has now produced six victories in six games in all competitions, including the Community Shield. No one, though, should be deceived by the emphasis lent to the scoreline by Bukayo Saka’s stoppage-time penalty; this was most definitely the toughest test this term for Arsenal.

If Sunderland can keep playing like this, Régis Le Bris and his players should have real cause for optimism – even if they could have done without Reinildo’s late sending-off for felling Saka when conceding that penalty and collecting a second yellow card.

His penalty miss aside, chapeaux off to Le Fee, who has deservedly made Zinedine Zidane’s provisional France squad for the forthcoming Nations League matches. Sunderland’s attacking playmaker knew another good performance here could only enhance his chances of moving from longlist to shortlist and he did not take long to draw a foul and win a dangerous free-kick.

View image in fullscreen Players tussle in the Sunderland penalty area during a even first half. Photograph: Lee Smith/Action Images/Reuters

Arsenal’s former captain Granit Xhaka delighted in curling the meanest of dead balls in Dan Ballard’s direction but the home central defender, a one-time Gunners youth captain, could not quite connect.

There had been a similar reprieve for Le Bris’s rearguard when Saka failed to make the most of Declan Rice’s fine early delivery. Yet, bar a Gabriel Magalhães shot from distance that whizzed just wide of Roefs’s goal, a Kai Havertz shot on the turn saved smartly and a low 20-yard effort that Le Fée dragged fractionally wide of an upright, that was pretty much it in terms of first-half goalmouth action.

Mikel Arteta’s side were taking their time to establish a settled passing rhythm. If Sunderland’s superb organisation hardly assisted the visiting cause, Arsenal looked a little fazed whenever the outstanding Nordi Mukiele – surely another candidate for the France squad – advanced from right-back.

Ezri Konsa, meanwhile, did not appear to be either relishing or winning his extremely physical contest with Le Bris’s ever-combative centre-forward, Brian Brobbey. If a packed Stadium of Light enjoyed that little subplot, the roof was nearly lifted off by the roar of approval that greeted Reinildo’s full-blooded early challenge on Martin Ødegaard.

View image in fullscreen Mikel Arteta is booked by John Brooks for leaving his technical area. Photograph: Lee Smith/Action Images/Reuters

One constant was Arteta’s excursions outside his technical area and eventually the referee, John Brooks, responded by jogging over to the touchline and waving a yellow card in the Arsenal manager’s face. While that booking was hardly unmerited, it seemed a shame that Brooks turned a blind eye to some persistent shirt-pulling from both sides at corners.

With the match even at the interval, Arteta replaced Myles Lewis-Skelly and the hobbling Ben White with Guimarães and Jurriën Timber. The Brazilian’s past as Newcastle’s captain ensured Guimarães’s every touch was booed, while Sunderland started the new half strongly, with Brobbey continuing to bully Konsa.

A penalty area encounter with Ballard at a throw proved no more welcome and when Konsa grappled the defender to the ground, Brooks – much to Arteta’s chagrin – had no hesitation in pointing to the spot.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

View image in fullscreen Bruno Guimarães, who had been jeered by Sunderland fans for being a former Newcastle player, taunts them after scoring. Photograph: Scott Heppell/Reuters

Le Fée attempted to squeeze his kick just inside an upright but Raya, excellent throughout, guessed correctly and tipped the ball quite brilliantly on to the woodwork. Talk about a sliding-doors moment. Two minutes later and very much against the run of play, Arsenal broke from another Sunderland throw and Guimarães did the rest.

With no option but to take risks, Le Bris switched to 4-4-2 and also introduced Malick Fofana, newly signed from Lyon, and he quickly created chaos in Arsenal’s box.

Although it took Roefs, who saved superbly from Saka, and Ballard, responsible for a vital header off the line, to keep Le Bris’s side in the game, while Timber had a headed “goal” disallowed for offside, Arteta had reason to look slightly nervous as Mukiele volleyed Le Fée’s corner over the bar.

By now Xhaka, booked for sliding into Guimarães, was enjoying himself in midfield and from one of his corners Mukiele again went close.

A comeback beckoned but Saka had different ideas as Arsenal issued a reminder that they will not surrender their title lightly.

Sports.title: De Zerbi says Spurs have ‘mental block’ after wait for league win continues
Sports.content:
Roberto De Zerbi says his Tottenham players continue to lack physical fitness and must “unblock” themselves in psychological terms after they drew their latest Premier League blank in a home 0-0 with Everton. It is now four games in the competition since the start of the season without a goal for Spurs; they sit 17th in the table with two points and were booed off by frustrated fans.

De Zerbi gave a number of explanations for Spurs’ slow start, chief among them the injuries that a clutch of players sustained on the long-haul pre-season tour to New Zealand and Australia. He lamented the impact of the World Cup on the return dates of certain players and mentioned how Sávio and Omar Marmoush had signed late in the transfer window.

De Zerbi talked up a positive opening 30 minutes from his players against Everton but accepted they ran out of steam and that there was a psychological problem.

“There is a word in Italian – sbloccarsi – that literally translates as if we unblock ourselves,” De Zerbi said. “[It is] a mental block because four games, no wins, no goals scored … it is tough for the players. The team is extremely strong, we can score goals and we can win games. And then we have to respect the history of the players in their careers. Forget Dominic Solanke and Marmoush – the other players … they didn’t score many, many goals in their careers and we have to find these goals. I think we can do so with the quality of our play.”

De Zerbi warmed to a familiar theme when he went back to the pre-season tour. “I said we started this season late for many, many reasons; too late,” he said. “Many players at the World Cup, many injuries, many problems in Australia. Micky van de Ven suffered an injury in Australia. Domi Solanke the same. James Maddison the same. Mateus Fernandes suffered an injury in Australia. He lost 15 days and it’s not so quick. Sávio and Marmoush, they came 10 days ago. I started to work with this [whole] group not last Thursday but two Thursdays ago. So, I think we have not the right physical condition yet.

“We played very well in the first 30 minutes and then maybe the energy, maybe the fact we didn’t score … maybe we lost in some players a little confidence. We have to be not positive but realistic.
