World.title: Rijeka Gateway Establishes Cooperation With Huge Shipping Companies
World.content:
September the 13th, 2026 – In its first year of commercial operation, Rijeka Gateway has successfully established cooperation with the two largest shipping companies in the world, Maersk and Hapag-Lloyd.

Sinisa Malus reports for Poslovni that the terminal has received more than a thousand trains and over 80 thousand trucks since opening, and the current ratio of cargo transport from the terminal is 42 percent by rail and 58 percent by road. Rijeka Gateway is the technologically most advanced container terminal in this part of Europe, in the first year since the start of commercial operations has created a team of 422 employees, raised the terminal to a high level of operational excellence required by the global APM Terminals network, received over 100 ships and handled more than 370 thousand TEU of cargo.

Additionally, the terminal has strengthened Rijeka’s logistical position between large Asian ports and the Mediterranean within the Gemini shipping network, and new logistical routes have been opened so that Rijeka is connected by regular rail links with Serbia, Hungary and Austria, as well as with important ports on the Adriatic and in Italy, it was highlighted at a press conference organised on the occasion of the first anniversary of commercial operations of Rijeka Gateway.

In the first year of commercial operations, Rijeka Gateway successfully established cooperation with the two largest shipping companies in the world, Maersk and Hapag-Lloyd, both of which use this terminal as their transhipment hub for import and export cargo from Italy. Rijeka Gateway has additionally confirmed its role as a regional logistical hub for container traffic within the Adriatic and is currently the only terminal on the Adriatic that performs this type of operations within the Gemini network. Information indicates that the lowland railway project has finally received the long-desired “acceleration”, which is necessary due to the new phase of development of the Rijeka terminal.

the gemini network

Rijeka Gateway has also confirmed its role as a regional logistical hub for container traffic within the Adriatic and is currently the only terminal on the Adriatic that performs this type of operations within the Gemini network – an operational cooperation between the companies Maersk and Hapag-Lloyd, which covers seven main global trade routes and serves to accelerate and optimise traffic, and Rijeka Gateway is a key port of call within the Gemini cooperation on the line connecting large Asian ports with the Mediterranean. Thus Rijeka is additionally connected with Trieste, Venice, Ravenna and Ancona.

Three ships currently arrive at Rijeka Gateway weekly: one mother vessel on the Asia–Europe service and two smaller feeder vessels. The introduction of an additional feeder service for Ploče and Durrës is expected soon. The terminal has also started parallel operations, which means that two smaller feeder vessels, around 150 metres in length, can be berthed in parallel at the terminal, and operations on them take place in parallel, which enables better utilisation of the operational quay, shorter waiting times for ships and greater efficiency of terminal operations.

“Rijeka has always had a vision and the port has always been the one that carried new development moments. We are striving for the connection of the Port of Rijeka with a double-track railway to go as quickly as possible, and for the container terminals to get an exit with the most efficient part of extracting traffic from the port. This port is not only a local and national interest, it has always been a European hub, and Rijeka Gateway contributes precisely to such positioning of Rijeka,” said Nina Perko, Director of the Maritime Administration in the Ministry of the Sea, Transport and Infrastructure.

Denis Vukorepa, Director of the Port Authority of Rijeka, recalled that thanks to Rijeka Gateway the total container traffic in the Port of Rijeka in the first six months of this year increased by 66 percent, and total traffic by around 40 percent.

“A year ago here we spoke about what Rijeka Gateway would mean for Rijeka, Croatia and this transport route. Today we see concrete results. In less than a year the terminal has received its hundredth ship, opened more than 420 new jobs and confirmed that Rijeka is once again strongly written on the map of European and world logistical flows. Rijeka Gateway represents the foundation for the further development of the port and an important step forward for the economy of Rijeka and Croatia,” said Denis Vukorepa, Director of the Port Authority of Rijeka.

“Rijeka has always been connected with the port, the port is part of our identity and part of our future. That is why it is important to us that our port is competitive, well connected with European and world markets. We are especially pleased that the development of the terminal brings new jobs, new knowledge, and especially opportunities for young people and the fact that young people can build their knowledge and experience right in our city. We want a Rijeka that develops, attracts such investments, creates new opportunities, new jobs, but a city in which development takes place with respect for space and the quality of life of our citizens,” emphasised Vedran Vivoda, Deputy Mayor of the City of Rijeka.

The terminal has received more than a thousand trains and over 80 thousand trucks since opening, and the current ratio of cargo transport from the terminal is 42 percent by rail and 58 percent by road.

corridors, ecology and employees

During the first year of terminal operations, more than 92 thousand hours of education and professional training were invested in employee development. This was preceded by an intensive period of learning and preparation, during which in 2025, ahead of the terminal’s launch, 130 thousand hours of education were recorded.

“When we draw a line under the first year of operations, I must say that I am most proud of three things. The first is our team of 422 employees, and that a young team considering that the average age of employees is 35 years, but also a team in which 20 percent are women, employed in almost all functions and levels of management. In Rijeka, and even in the wider region, such a technologically advanced terminal did not exist, our jobs and processes are special and very complex, so building a team that can compete at that level with the best terminals is a source of pride not only for all of us at Rijeka Gateway, but also for Rijeka and the whole of Croatia.

The second are the new logistical corridors with which we have connected Rijeka with the region, which is a great value that our terminal has brought. The third is that we have continued to carefully monitor our impact on the environment and the community with the goal of being a good neighbour to the citizens of Rijeka. We have successfully certified the environmental management system according to the ISO 14001:2015 standard, confirming our commitment to environmental protection, and we continuously communicate with the local community on all topics related to the quality of life of citizens,” said Peter Corfitsen, President of the Management Board of Rijeka Gateway.

The terminal has received more than a thousand trains and over 80 thousand trucks since opening, and the current ratio of cargo transport from the terminal is 42 percent by rail and 58 percent by road. The entry and exit process for truck transport is fully digitised, which speeds up the truck processing process and reduces waiting times, which reduces the burden on traffic and pollution. The average truck time is around 15 minutes, and the shortest achieved truck processing time is ten minutes, and that on a day when more than 500 trucks were processed.

It is clear that the main limitation remains the railway. In this year little has changed. Nevertheless, information indicates that the project has finally received the long-desired “acceleration”, primarily bureaucratic. The project practically languished unprepared for years, only to receive the necessary acceleration in the past year. Processes have been moved from a standstill, so it is still to be expected that by the middle of the next decade we will finally see the realisation of that project.

investments for rijeka and the community

“By handling 370 thousand TEU of cargo we have significantly raised the total capacity of the Port of Rijeka and we are rapidly approaching the numbers we planned – and that is to reach a handling of 650 thousand TEU, and then in the second phase one million TEU. During the first year of operations Rijeka Gateway maintained a high level of operational reliability, with 98 percent availability of port equipment and 99 percent availability of key systems on the operational quay and storage areas, which is at the level of the best terminals.

For the full potential of the terminal, the planned increase in the capacity of rail traffic will be key and here we welcome the activities of the Government of the Republic of Croatia. We will continue to invest in the local community, especially through cooperation with the Faculty of Maritime Studies and the University of Rijeka, through various scholarship and education programmes, but also through donation programmes aimed at Rijeka kindergartens and primary schools,” concluded Tomislav Rosandić, Member of the Management Board of Rijeka Gateway.

World.title: Croatian Airports Enjoy a Record Summer
World.content:
September the 13th, 2026 – Croatian airports have enjoyed a record summer this year, with July in particular standing out.

Croatian airports recorded strong passenger traffic in July 2026. A total of 2,355 thousand passengers passed through domestic airports, which is 40 thousand more than in the same month last year. Zrinka Gabelica Toplek reports for Poslovni that when compared to July 2025, when 2,315 thousand passengers passed through Croatian airports, this year’s result is an increase of 1.7 percent. The largest number of passengers was recorded by Split Airport, through which 767 thousand passengers passed in July, thus retaining the status of the busiest Croatian airport.

It is followed by Dubrovnik Airport with 557 thousand passengers, while 465 thousand passengers passed through Zagreb Airport. In fourth place is Zadar Airport with 365 thousand passengers, and fifth place was taken by Pula Airport with 145 thousand passengers.

split comes out on top

In July 2026, 2.35 million passengers passed through Croatian airports, which is 1.7% more than in the same month last year, and Split was the busiest. The five busiest airports together recorded 2,299 thousand passenger movements, or almost the entire traffic recorded at Croatian airports during July.

According to the country of origin of passengers, the most passengers arrived from Germany, from which 380 thousand passengers were recorded. The German market was thus the most important source of passenger traffic in the Croatian air system. In second place was the United Kingdom with 376 thousand passengers, while 192 thousand passengers were recorded from Poland in July. France follows with 180 thousand passengers.

The four leading markets – Germany, the United Kingdom, Poland and France – together accounted for 1,128 thousand passengers, which shows how important a role European markets play in Croatian air traffic during the main tourist season.

World.title: This Dalmatian Island is Heavily Visited, But Few Spend the Night There…
World.content:
September the 12th, 2026 – There’s a beautiful Dalmatian island that attracts around 150,000 visitors each summer, but only 40 or so of them opt to actually spend the night there.

Gorgeous Biševo itself had only 44 registered tourists in 2025, while more than 150,000 people visited the famous Blue Cave. Putni kofer writes that at first glance, Biševo in the middle of summer is anything but a deserted island. Boats full of day-trippers arrive all day long, people wait to board the small boats that transport thousands towards the world-famous Blue Cave. According to currently available data, during the summer, over 150,000 tourists visit the cave, and one of the most famous natural attractions on the Adriatic brings a huge number of people to this small open-sea island every year.

However, most of them board the boat again after visiting the Blue Cave and leave, heading off elsewhere. Few stay to explore the rest of the island. During the whole of 2025, according to data from the Croatian Bureau of Statistics, only 44 people decided to actually spend the night on Biševo.

a contrast unlike any other on the adriatic coast

Day-trippers arrive on Biševo from nearby Komiža, but also from Split, Hvar and the surrounding islands, as well as numerous coastal tourist destinations. The visit to the Blue Cave itself lasts less than half an hour, but on the island it is also possible to visit the Visitor Centre inland, the old military tunnels, and to swim on beautiful beaches such as the one in the place of Porat. It is a real shame to reduce a trip to Biševo only to a visit to the cave. But most people visit it that way, which is confirmed by both statistics and our experience: when we continued exploring the island after viewing the most famous attraction, we met perhaps twenty people during the whole day.

This contrast between the number of visitors and those who stay on the island at least a little longer is unique in Croatia. It is not only a matter of overnight stays: after all, only about thirty beds are registered on Biševo. The island is ideal for a full-day excursion, swimming, getting to know the heritage, which many skip because they concentrate only on the famous cave. This is also confirmed by a study by the Institute for Tourism. Their research showed that only 8.3 percent of guests stay eight hours or longer on the island, and almost half said they came exclusively because of the Blue Cave.

The Blue Cave in Balun bay owes its name to the reflection of the sun’s rays which around noon, in calm seas, penetrate through an underwater opening into the cave, reflecting off the white bottom and creating the blue colour. It is 24 metres long and about 12 metres wide, and its modest depth of 3 to 20 metres and typical karst shape make it an ideal habitat for a diverse ecosystem, while divers discover its mysterious world through hidden underwater cracks. It is said that it is best to visit it between 11:00 and 14:00 on a sunny day.

no shop, no cash machine, and no maritime connections…

The island of Biševo is the most remote inhabited Croatian island. It stands proudly in the middle of the open sea, isolated and a little wild, and a holiday on it is definitely not for everyone. Neither ferries nor catamarans sail to it, and it is connected to neighbouring Vis by the only boat line, Sv. Salvestar, the so-called “pruga”, which departs from Komiža. It spans only 5.8 square kilometres, in the middle of the last century about 300 inhabitants lived on it, and today only about ten remain. Biševo was once known as the home of the Mediterranean monk seal, but that animal disappeared from the island long ago. Besides the most famous Blue Cave, on the southern side of the island, in Trešjavac bay, there is also the beautiful Medvidina Cave. The island also has its own distinctive wine: Biševo plavac.

the home of caves, military tunnels and stunning beaches

In the very centre of the island a few years ago the Visitor Centre was opened, which you can reach from Mezoporat harbour by electric cart. The Centre is really worth visiting; it presents the wonderful world of underwater, terrestrial and geological phenomena, and also showcases the rich past of the island. The surroundings are also interesting: an old village with a beautiful church that was probably once full of life. The military tunnels are located at the other end of the island, on Cape Gatula, and if you are not up for walking, you can specially arrange transport by electric vehicles to them.

A walk that is definitely worth it is the one from the Visitor Centre to the place of Porat, where the regular boat line docks and can take you directly back to Komiža from there. Porat beach is, according to many, one of the most beautiful on the Adriatic. Soft sand, enough shade, a café for refreshment… Although there are day-trippers, the crowds are practically never too big. This island is isolated and certainly not for everyone, but it is a real glimpse of genuine Dalmatian island life that is rapidly being sent to the history books on other islands.

World.title: Meet the Highest Fortress of the Dubrovnik Republic… That Isn’t Even in Dubrovnik
World.content:
September the 12th, 2026 – The highest fortress of the former Dubrovnik Republic (Ragusa) isn’t even located within the city. It’s a very unusual, irregular fortification that once played a vitally important defensive role.

Nestled against the rock sits one of the most monumental fortification systems in the south of Croatia, and it was once an important cog in the defence of the powerful Republic of Dubrovnik. Putni kofer writes that anyone who looks at Dubrovnik clearly sees that this city is teeming with incredible history. Even without any prior knowledge, the gaze will stop on the monumental walls, fortresses, palaces… Today one of the most beautiful cities on the Mediterranean, it was once a powerful force. The Dubrovnik Republic was small in a territorial sense, but politically, commercially and diplomatically, it was extremely influential.

Lovrijenac, Revelin, Minčeta, Bokar and St. John are fortresses that line up in the defensive ring of the city or next to it, but none of these fortresses was the largest defensive fortification of the powerful republic. It is located about forty kilometres from the city, among the hills of Konavle. Sokol Grad is, according to official sources, the largest single fortress from the time of the Republic of Dubrovnik.

sokol grad towers on a natural 25-metre rock

Sokol Grad was built above the small place of Dunave, on a natural rock that rises more than 25 metres above the surrounding terrain. Its walls so faithfully follow the shape of the rock and blend in colour with the karst that from a distance the fortress looks almost like its extension. The position was not chosen for beauty, although the view today is spectacular. From this point the Konavle field and an important road that led from the hinterland towards Dubrovnik were monitored, and official sources state that from Sokol one of the most complete views of the entire Konavle opens up.

a hillfort existed there all the way back to prehistoric times

The fortress did not originate in the time of the Dubrovnik Dubrovnik. Traces have been found in this area that point to much older fortification of the position, from a prehistoric hillfort through ancient and late antique fortifications. It is mentioned in written documents at the end of the 14th century, and at the beginning of the 15th century its Dubrovnik story begins. The people of Dubrovnik briefly entered the fortress in 1420, and from 1423 it came under their control again and remained part of their defensive system for the next two and a half centuries. Its task was clear: to protect Konavle from enemies who could arrive from the hinterland. Precisely for this reason the Republic of Dubrovnik did not spare on its maintenance. During the 15th century the walls were repaired, expanded and strengthened, and construction works continued in the 16th and 17th centuries. Sokol also protected an area of vital economic importance, including the area of the river Ljuta and the mills that participated in the supply of Dubrovnik.

a three-level fortress

Sokol Grad has an irregular shape and that is no coincidence. The ramparts follow the morphology of the rock, and the entire fortification is organised on three levels. The lowest part, called Kamen (Stone), was arranged as a space into which the surrounding population could take shelter in case of danger. In the outer bailey were the fortified main entrance, kitchen, food stores, rooms for soldiers and crossbowmen, a guard tower and sanitary facilities.

The safest part was at the very top. In the citadel there was a large cistern, stores of food and weapons, grain supplies, the castellan’s residence, a church, a blacksmith’s workshop and a furnace. The system for sheltering the population was precisely determined: children under the age of ten were to be housed in the upper fortress in case of danger, while women and those unfit for combat were housed in the outer bailey.

it survived the devastating 1667 earthquake

Sokol survived the great earthquake of 1667, but after 1672 it is no longer mentioned in the Dubrovnik archival records, so it is considered that it was abandoned at that time. For centuries it decayed, and the surrounding population used its stone as building material. The Society of Friends of Dubrovnik Antiquities took it over in 1966, after which decades of conservation and restoration followed. Intensive works lasted from 2007 to 2013, when Sokol Grad was reopened to visitors. Today, instead of guards on its walls, there are day-trippers, and the former military position has become one of the best viewpoints in Konavle. Sokol Grad is open to visitors, and in the current period the official website lists opening hours from 08:00 to 19:00; tickets can also be purchased online and the price is 10 euros for adults and 5 euros for children.

World.title: Croatia is the Only EU Country Without a Waste Incinerator
World.content:
September the 12th, 2026 – After the hazardous waste scandal in Lika comes the news that Croatia is actually the only EU country without a proper waste incinerator.

Croatia is facing an enormous waste management problem with nowhere left to dispose of it, and at the same time it is the only EU Member State without a single waste incinerator. Index reports that all across the rest of Europe, more than 500 of them are currently operating. Switzerland, Norway, the UK and others also have numerous incinerators. After the scandal involving improperly disposed waste in Gospić, the question of building energy plants, facilities for the thermal treatment of waste, is being raised once again.

After the horrific case in Gospić, it seems the question is no longer whether Croatia can avoid thermal treatment of waste, but where it will even carry it out. Landfills have limited capacity, and European rules require less and less landfilling of waste that can be treated differently.

croatian ministers are confused

Minister of Economy Ante Šušnjar points out that Croatian companies are building such facilities across Europe. “If all EU Member States have them, only Malta does not but is building them, and if there are 500 of them, is Croatia the smartest or is there some other issue here? When it comes to building incinerators, Croatian companies today are building them across Europe, in Iceland, Belgium, Scotland and Germany. If we can do that for the whole world, I think we should also do it here,” said Šušnjar, as reported by N1.

Energy plants burn waste and use the resulting energy to produce electricity and heating. They are not a replacement for recycling, but a solution for the remaining part of the waste. Their construction in Croatia has for years been opposed by part of the public due to concerns about emissions, impacts on health and the environment, and the disposal of residues after incineration.

Minister of Environmental Protection Marija Vučković believes that the set waste management targets cannot be achieved without energy plants. “Would I accept an energy plant in my neighbourhood? If the environmental impact assessment has shown that it is acceptable, if the conditions from the permits are regularly controlled and, of course, if the supervision system is fully functional, there is no reason not to have an energy plant in one’s neighbourhood,” said Vučković.

is the system the problem?

Nikola Grmoja from Most sees the problem in the system, not in the disposal model itself. “If we do not have a control system, if hazardous waste could be imported into Croatia without anyone noticing or doing anything about it, how will we know what is being burned there, where it is being brought from, what the by-product is and where that by-product ends up?” asks Grmoja. He believes this is a question of a non-functioning system and corrupt people in key positions. “If we talk about the model, I am not sure how incinerators fit into all the goals that the European Commission has set for us regarding waste separation,” he said.

the zagreb project and interest from other cities

Interest in building energy plants has been shown by Šibenik, Osijek and Rijeka, and Zagreb is also considering it. A feasibility projection for Zagreb was made back in 2024 and showed that such facilities pay off. President of the Zagreb City Assembly Matej Mišić confirmed the position of the city SDP to N1. “The city SDP continues to advocate the construction of an energy plant that would burn refuse-derived fuel and thereby generate thermal energy. In fact, the City Assembly already in 2024 adopted a conclusion launching the preparation of documentation for the construction of an energy plant,” said Mišić. Although the project was started, it has not been realised. If energy plants become part of the solution for waste in Croatia, the open question remains whether the need for waste disposal will ultimately outweigh the resistance to such facilities.

World.title: New 14,000 Square Metre Shopping Mecca for Croatia
World.content:
September the 12th, 2026 – A new 14,000 square metre shopping mecca for Croatia has opened up more shopping and job opportunities near Samobor.

The opening of the new complex is a significant contribution to the local labour market and new employment opportunities for the residents of Samobor and the surrounding area, stated Joško Piteša, Director of Operations for Croatia. The 22nd retail park of this type is opening in Croatia; it will offer 23 well-known brands and around a hundred jobs. Poslovni reports that Samobor has now become richer with another shopping mecca. On 14,318 square metres of sales space, the Stop Shop retail park is being officially opened. This is already the 22nd concept of this type in Croatia, and it will offer 23 well-known brands, 429 parking spaces, and it should also be noted that each new location is expected to create around 100 new jobs.

a contribution to the local market

“This is our largest location in Croatia so far, so we expect the number of jobs to be even higher than the average of our network. It is certainly a significant contribution to the local labor market and new employment opportunities for the residents of Samobor and the surrounding area,” says Joško Piteša, Director of Operations for Croatia. The doors are being opened by well-known domestic and international brands such as TEDi, Mana Moda, LC Waikiki, Plodine, CCC, BabyCenter, Sinsay, Action, Optika Anda, Vitapur, dm, Znanje, Bipa, NKD, Admiral Bar, The Fitness, Le Mas, Zoo City, s’Oliver, Vacom, Europa 92, Mambino and Sport Vision.

expansion and development

By the end of the year, projects in Bjelovar and the expansion of the park in Vinkovci will continue. This opening in Samobor is a continuation of the brand’s expansion on the Croatian market, and Piteša says that they do not view the new location exclusively through the prism of competition with the existing offer, but as its complement.

“Our advantage is in the concept of simple and practical shopping – good traffic accessibility, parking, direct access to stores and the possibility of doing different types of shopping in one location. We expect that precisely this combination of diverse offer, accessibility and practicality will make Stop Shop Samobor attractive not only to the residents of the city, but also to customers from the wider surrounding area,” he says, adding that by the end of this year they will continue with the planned projects in Bjelovar and the expansion of the existing retail park in Vinkovci.

He also emphasised that ambitions on the Croatian market do not stop there and that they intend to continue expanding the network in the coming years, especially in areas where they recognize the need for a practical retail offer. “Croatia remains an important market for us with potential for further investments and development.”

The retail park concept has proven to be extremely resilient and popular with customers, so we ask whether he sees saturation of this model in the future or room for more? “Previous experience shows that on the Croatian market there is still interest from both customers and tenants, but we believe that further development must be thoughtful and based on the real needs of each local market. We do not believe in expansion just for the sake of increasing the number of locations – each project must have a clearly defined catchment area, appropriate traffic infrastructure, a quality mix of tenants and long-term potential.”

Stop Shop in Croatia systematically chooses medium-sized cities, so we ask what they expect from Samobor? “The focus on medium-sized cities is an integral part of our concept and long-term development strategy. Precisely in cities like Samobor we see space for accessible retail content that enables residents to do a large part of their shopping in their immediate vicinity,” he says, adding that the goal is not to concentrate the offer exclusively in the largest urban centres, but to bring retail infrastructure closer to customers in smaller and medium-sized cities. “Samobor fits very well into this strategy thanks to its size, economic activity, good traffic connections and proximity to Zagreb, but also a strong local community and a wider catchment area,” he concludes.

World.title: Records Broken as Croatia Surpasses 5 Million Arrivals in August
World.content:
September the 11th, 2026 – Records have been broken as Croatia successfully surpasses 5 million arrivals in August alone.

A staggering 17.5 million arrivals and 90.5 million overnight stays were recorded across Croatia during the first eight months of this year. That impressive figure represents a 1% increase in both indicators compared to the same period last year, the Croatian Tourist Board announced. Index reports that of the total number of overnight stays realised, 86.7 million were registered on the coast and islands and 3.8 million on the mainland. Data from the eVisitor system also show that in August alone, for the first time in history, the number of more than five million tourist arrivals in a single month was exceeded. This is according to a statement from the Ministry of Tourism and Sport and the Croatian Tourist Board.

an expectation-shattering august this year

In August alone, more than five million guests arrived in Croatia, which is 2% more than in the same month last year. 31.4 million overnight stays were recorded, or half a percent more than in last year’s August. The most overnight stays in the eighth month were recorded by guests from Germany, Croatia, Slovenia, Poland, Austria, Italy, Hungary and the Czech Republic. By counties, Istria, Split-Dalmatia and Kvarner lead, while the most visited destinations were Rovinj, Vir, Poreč, Medulin, Umag and Dubrovnik.

“Croatian tourism is competitive, which is evident from all indicators, and we have done our utmost for that. Behind us are an extraordinary eight months and a summer season in which, despite numerous challenges, we achieved growth in key indicators,” said Minister of Tourism and Sport Tonči Glavina.

“It’s particularly important that we achieved this result in circumstances of changed travel habits. We have constantly said that trips would be shorter and that guests would manage their budgets more rationally, and the difference between the growth in arrivals and the somewhat milder growth in overnight stays precisely confirms this,” he added. The minister thanked the entire tourism sector for their cooperation and readiness to respond to seasonal challenges, especially regarding price competitiveness.

detailed results for the first 8 months of 2026

Looking by counties, in the period from January to the end of August, the most overnight stays were recorded in Istria, 25.4 million. This is followed by Split-Dalmatia County with more than 17 million overnight stays and Kvarner with 15.2 million. The most visited destinations in the year so far were Rovinj, Dubrovnik, Poreč, Split, Umag and Medulin. The most numerous guests in the first eight months were Germans with 16.9 million overnight stays. Domestic guests recorded 11.7 million overnight stays, followed by guests from Slovenia (9.6 million), Austria (6.3 million), Poland (6.3 million), the Czech Republic (4.5 million), Hungary (3.7 million), Italy (3.5 million) and the United Kingdom (3.2 million).

plans for the remainder of 2026

Director of the Croatian Tourist Board Kristjan Staničić emphasized that the results confirm strong interest in Croatia. “As a destination, Croatia has responded very well to market challenges and changes in traveller behaviour, who today make decisions about travel much more carefully. I believe that, in addition to the quality of the offer and the work of the entire sector, the continuity of our promotional activities has also contributed to this,” said Staničić. He noted that the HTZ was active in key markets through digital campaigns, social networks, PR activities and cooperation with carriers and tour operators.

“An important part of the year remains ahead of us and we are very focused on the off-season and the winter period. We want to maintain positive momentum, but at the same time continue working on quality, competitiveness and greater value of Croatian tourism,” concluded Staničić.

World.title: Alutaguse National Park to expand by nearly 25,000 hectares
World.content:
The government has approved amendments to the protection rules for Alutaguse National Park, aimed at merging existing protected areas and species habitats into a single functioning whole. The park will expand by 24,749 hectares, bringing its total area to 69,768 hectares.

"Alutaguse is Estonia's largest continuous forest‑and‑bog landscape and the only place where the flying squirrel still lives. Current protection is fragmented: small core areas in the middle of managed forest have not improved the species' status. With the expansion, we are connecting these isolated fragments into a functioning whole," said Minister of Energy and Environment Andres Sutt.

Linking the park's existing, separated parcels and nearly one hundred small core areas into an ecologically coherent forest mass is essential for strengthening protection of two umbrella species — the flying squirrel and the capercaillie.

The expansion takes place almost entirely on state land: of the newly protected areas, only 24 hectares — about 0.1 percent — are privately owned. This private land will fall under a limited‑management zone where forestry remains possible under certain conditions.

The national park will incorporate 97 previously separate species core areas totaling 7,506 hectares, and an additional 17,237 hectares will be protected for the first time. Most of this consists of valuable forest habitats. Protection will also extend to 3,040 hectares of previously unprotected bogs, including Virunurme bog and the Lemmaku, Kaasiku, Kassisaare, Õpetaja and Pikasilla bogs.

Alutaguse National Park after the expansion. Source: Ministry of Climate

The flying squirrel's range in Estonia is limited to Alutaguse, and the species is in critical condition. Existing core areas are 25‑meter circles around nest trees. Because flying squirrels glide rather than fly, they require continuous canopy cover. If surrounding forest is cut, the protected circle becomes an island in an open clearing — leaving the animal without food sources or movement corridors. This isolates small populations that eventually die out. The same logic applies to capercaillie and other species dependent on old forests: what matters is not the number of patches but whether they are connected.

Capercaillie habitat will gain an additional 10,513 hectares of protection. Alutaguse is one of Estonia's most important capercaillie strongholds. In total, the expansion improves protection for 37 threatened or declining species.

Experience from neighboring countries such as Lithuania and Finland shows that expanding national parks has a positive impact on nature tourism and the service sector that depends on it.

Alutaguse features Estonia's only mainland dunes, the lake‑rich Kurtna landscape, the longest sandy beach on Lake Peipus, and Puhatu — one of Northern Europe's largest bog complexes. National‑park status signals internationally that the region has high‑quality visitor infrastructure for exploring natural values.

Metsis. Autor/allikas: RMK

RMK is building Estonia's first treetop nature trail in Kauksi and renovating the Kauksi recreation area. A nature spa recently opened in Uusküla, and development activity has increased in the holiday‑home areas along Peipus's northern shore. Together with existing attractions and accommodation, the expansion supports longer visitor stays even outside the summer peak season.

The procedure was launched by the climate minister's directive on 17 October 2024, and the draft protection rules were publicly displayed from 18 June to 5 September 2025. Based on submitted proposals, restrictions in the capercaillie zone were eased, 1.7 hectares of residential land were removed from protection, and construction was permitted on yard land. The regulation enters into force on the tenth day after publication in the Riigi Teataja.

ERR reported in April that the expansion had been delayed. Nearly six years ago, the Estonian Fund for Nature proposed expanding the park. The state intended to finally make the long‑delayed decision — even without municipal support if necessary, as Alutaguse municipality had long opposed the expansion.

When then‑climate minister Yoko Alender launched the expansion at the Iisaku Nature Center in autumn 2024, the aim was to complete the process within six months.

World.title: ECB rate hike could push loan payments higher next spring
World.content:
The European Central Bank's latest rate hike is already reflected in the six‑month Euribor that shapes most Estonians' loan payments, meaning borrowers are unlikely to see higher monthly costs this year — but a spring increase could still push payments up.

Financial markets currently believe that Thursday's ECB rate hike to 2.5 percent will not be the last this year.

"Market expectations put euro‑area base rates at around 2.8 percent by year‑end, and by next spring they are expected to rise to about 3.2 percent. Euribor, which moves mainly according to market expectations, stands at 2.8 percent today," said Rain Leesi, head of investments at Avaron, an investment management firm.

Since the six‑month Euribor affecting Estonians' loan payments is already at 2.8 percent, the next rate hike is considered priced in and should not raise loan payments. A further rise in Euribor is more likely later on.

"If we look at the level at which Euribor can be fixed for the next five years, today it can be fixed at 3.5 percent — the same high rate as in 2023, when ECB interest rates were around four percent," Leesi said.

Most Estonian home‑loan contracts use floating Euribor, meaning any rise in Euribor directly affects monthly payments.

"If today the six‑month Euribor is 2.8 percent and it rises by half a percentage point, then for a €100,000 loan balance the monthly payment increases by €30, and for €150,000 by €45," said Sille Hallang, head of retail banking at SEB.

So far, rising Euribor has not dampened Estonians' appetite for home loans.

"We do not see a decline in borrower activity — quite the opposite. The home‑loan market is very active and growing compared with last year, so there is no visible direct impact at the moment," Hallang said.

According to Hallang, SEB's volume of new home loans has grown more than 10 percent over the past year.

Ülo Kaasik, governor of Eesti Pank and member of the ECB Governing Council, said he understands why markets expect further rate hikes, noting that they depend on global developments and energy‑price movements.

"Whether we need to raise rates further depends on how future developments unfold and how inflation pressures play out. The main concern now is that risks are increasing, especially geopolitical risks, where events can shift in either direction at any moment," Kaasik said.

World.title: Tallinn to open exhibition of Masayoshi Sukita's David Bowie portraits
World.content:
Starting 9 October, the Poco Art Museum will present Japanese photographer Masayoshi Sukita's solo exhibition dedicated to pop‑music legend David Bowie — marking the first time Sukita's work is shown in Estonia.

The exhibition features more than one hundred photographs highlighting the 40‑year creative partnership between Bowie and Sukita. The show arrives in Tallinn from its previous European tour stop in Gothenburg.

"'Bowie x Sukita' has travelled through some of the world's largest museums and cultural institutions. Its arrival in Tallinn is the strongest confirmation yet that Poco has reached an international level, operating alongside the world's leading art institutions. And more importantly: the Tallinn public deserves access to world‑class art in their own city," said Poco founder Linnar Viik.

Masayoshi Sukita encountered Bowie in an unusual way: he did not speak English, and Bowie did not speak Japanese. But upon seeing a Bowie poster on a London street in 1972, Sukita immediately knew he had to photograph him. Sukita followed Bowie across the world — from Tokyo press conferences to Berlin studio sessions, the streets of Kyoto and concert stages in New York.

"Bowie x Sukita x Poco" will remain open until 25 April next year.

World.title: Small parties face steep deposit hurdle in bid for Riigikogu seats
World.content:
Parties outside parliament are weighing bids for next spring's Riigikogu elections, with some already committing and others still undecided, but all face the same major hurdle: raising the candidate deposit required to get on the ballot.

The board of the Estonian Nationalists and Conservatives (EERK), founded in 2024 by former EKRE members, decided unanimously a few weeks ago that the party will participate in the March Riigikogu elections with its own list. EERK chair Rein Suurkask said the plan is to field lists in all electoral districts.

"The goal is to clear the electoral threshold — five percent. That is the main objective, and there's no room for doubt. We are of the view that we won't settle for less; that five percent is very important for us," Suurkask said.

EERK is currently assembling its lists, and the campaign is being prepared. The entire program will be based on the party's core principle that the state exists for its people, Suurkask added.

The Estonian Greens will also definitely participate in the Riigikogu elections, said party co‑leader Rasmus Lahtvee.

"For a political party, the most important goal is to participate in elections, gain a mandate, and then implement decisions based on its worldview," Lahtvee said.

However, Lahtvee sees the deposit requirement — which must be paid to register candidates — as a major challenge. The deposit equals one Estonian minimum monthly wage per candidate. According to initial calculations, the Greens may need around €120,000 if they run a full list.

"A party that is not funded by taxpayers must pay this amount itself, and if it doesn't get elected, it loses the money. In the European Parliament elections, the Greens went to court and received interim relief. There is still no final decision from Europe, but for those elections, the European Commission said the amount was clearly excessive," Lahtvee noted.

The Estonian National Liberals–Free Party has also recently contacted the Chancellor of Justice regarding the deposit issue. Party chair Märt Meesak said political competition should be more open.

"Half joking, if you don't have a rich mother‑in‑law handing you money from a cupboard or a wealthy uncle in America, it's pretty difficult. I think this is a serious problem for Estonian democracy, because this way we never get new people or new ideas. Right now, we're not checking the seriousness of candidates — only the thickness of their wallets — and that's not good for democracy," Meesak said.

Meesak added that although the party has become more active recently, the board will likely make a final decision on participating in the Riigikogu elections in November. By then, the Chancellor of Justice's response on the deposit issue should also be available, he said.

Last autumn, there was talk that Plan B might enter the Riigikogu elections as a party, but that plan has since collapsed. Plan B's Narva representative Urbo Vaarmann said the group will not participate with its own list. However, members may run as independents or on another party's list. Vaarmann added that Plan B aims to counter excessive party power and supports rethinking the party system.

World.title: Tallinn has 50 kilometers of walkable underground pipes
World.content:
Tallinna Vesi development manager Marti Vaksmann says that there are 3,000 kilometers of pipelines beneath Tallinn, including 50 kilometers of large pipes where a person can walk. He notes that being inside a wastewater collector is not the most pleasant experience, but it is part of the job.

Construction has been underway all summer at the Hipodroom intersection in Tallinn, and the reason for the repairs lies underground.

"We're going about four meters deep here, but in Tallinn some places reach depths of up to 30 meters," said Vaksmann, development manager for water and sewerage assets at Tallinna Vesi. "We've measured that Tallinn has 3,000 kilometers of pipelines, and about 50 kilometers of those are large enough for us to walk through."

The existing pipes were installed nearly a century ago, when Tallinn still used a combined sewer system, with stormwater and wastewater flowing through the same pipe. "Today we're building a separate stormwater pipeline right under the Hipodroom intersection. We're planning for the next 50 years, assuming rainfall may become more intense, so we won't need to rebuild this pipe again. If it seems to passersby that not much construction is happening at Hipodroom site, that's because most of it is underground," Vaksmann said.

Vaksmann said he likes pipes and doesn't feel afraid walking inside them. "Many people don't like tight spaces, but that's our job. Right now we're in a stormwater collector, but there are also wastewater collectors, and walking in those is not the most pleasant — but someone has to do it."

"In addition to the large pipelines, there's also a water pipe here, a sewer pipe, heating pipelines, and various cables under the sidewalks. Whenever possible, we shift pipelines under the sidewalk," Vaksmann explained. "There are no buildings directly above us."

World.title: Mari Roosvalt and Jaan Elken's joint exhibition sums up 25 years of work
World.content:
On 12 September, the Pärnu Museum of New Art will open "Dialoog" (Dialogue), a joint exhibition by painters Mari Roosvalt and Jaan Elken. The retrospective brings together works created by the two artists over the past 25 years.

"Perhaps some of our principles are similar. Elken has worked in acrylic, while I've mostly stayed with oil and built my approach around that. We share a certain common attitude toward this dialogue. Many of our themes overlap — ecological and political subjects. We follow the art field closely and pay attention to what's happening around us," said painter Mari Roosvalt.

"We have so many overlaps and so many opportunities for dialogue, and we're connected through technique. We're both painting innovators, and here we present a more forceful, robust kind of painting, full of life in the brushstrokes, palette‑knife marks, collaged elements, flags and slogans that make up the works. It's essentially a painting hybrid with echoes of early pop art. There were an incredible number of connections, so I truly enjoyed putting this exhibition together. I thank Mari for her trust," said painter Jaan Elken.

The exhibition at the Pärnu Museum of New Art (MONA) will remain open until 18 October.

World.title: Packaging rules for small businesses 'a problem we must tackle together', EU official says
World.content:
New EU packaging rules could saddle micro‑businesses with heavy costs and bureaucracy when selling across borders, prompting the European Commission to signal it may allow flexibility for the smaller firms, a senior official said during a visit to Estonia.

New extended producer‑responsibility requirements may make selling into another member state too costly and bureaucratic for very small companies, said Patrick Child, deputy director‑general of the European Commission's environment directorate.

The main goal of the EU packaging regulation is to reduce excessive packaging and packaging waste, promote reusable packaging and recycling, and harmonize standards across member states so the packaging sector can function more effectively at EU level. The aim is also to reduce the climate and environmental impact of packaging, support the single market and lessen Europe's dependence on imported raw materials. The agreed rules will take effect gradually.

In August, the provisions concerning hazardous substances in food‑contact packaging materials entered into force. Most requirements will apply starting in 2030.

The exact content of several rules — such as the ban on plastic packaging for fruit and vegetables under 1.5 kg — will be clarified through implementing acts now being drafted by the European Commission, taking into account input from member states, businesses and other stakeholders. "We must ensure the regulation does not hinder the functioning of the internal market; on the contrary, our aim is for rules to be more uniform across Europe," Child said.

Child visited Estonia this week to discuss two topics with authorities and stakeholders: EU circular‑economy proposals and implementation of the Nature Restoration Regulation. In the context of the packaging regulation, one question raised was how the new rules will affect small and medium‑sized enterprises operating across borders — specifically how companies will contribute to waste‑management costs in the future.

Some provisions have prompted concerns that they impose excessive administrative burdens and costs on companies. "We are discussing this with the aim of reaching a result that stimulates economic activity in EU countries and creates more jobs," Child said.

System needs more flexibility

Asked what changes companies should prepare for, Child said the new regulation followed extensive preparation and consultations with businesses. He stressed that the agreed requirements will not take effect overnight — the goal is a smooth, controlled transition.

"We already see that companies investing in new technologies and more sustainable packaging solutions, or developing them, are anticipating market developments and creating business opportunities for the future," he said.

Still, Child acknowledged that the system needs more flexibility so that micro‑ and small enterprises exporting to other member states — for example via online platforms — do not face excessive costs or administrative burdens. "This is a problem we must tackle together," he noted.

A year ago, the Commission proposed suspending the obligation to appoint and pay for an extended producer‑responsibility representative in another member state. "I understand that for micro‑enterprises this can be too expensive," Child said. He explained that the system should be based on mutual recognition between member states or exempt small companies from certain requirements. The proposal is currently under discussion among member states.

In Estonia, media attention has focused on the country's intention to introduce some requirements stricter than those in the EU regulation. "Generally, as long as national rules remain within what the legislation allows, higher environmental‑protection standards are acceptable to us," Child said.

Higher environmental standards welcomed

He added that each case must be assessed individually and Estonian laws reviewed. "But in principle, we welcome it when a member state has a higher level of environmental protection," Child said.

Regarding the packaging of unprocessed fresh fruit and vegetables and pre‑packed fresh produce under 1.5 kg, plastic packaging will be restricted starting 1 January 2030. This does not mean, for example, that cucumbers cannot be sold in packaging at all — the ban applies to certain types of single‑use plastic packaging.

Member states may grant exemptions if there is proven need — for example to prevent water loss, wilting, microbiological risks, physical damage or oxidation, or when mixing organic and conventional products cannot be avoided otherwise. The procedure for applying exemptions will be clarified.

"With fresh food and vegetables, we must be extremely careful with anything that could reduce product quality or pose risks to consumers," Child said.

World.title: Tallinn Half Marathon sees fastest times ever recorded
World.content:
Kenyan runners dominated the Tallinn Marathon half‑marathon on Saturday, winning both the men's and women's races and setting new event records.

More than 5,000 participants started the 21.1‑kilometer race at 9 a.m. on Saturday from Falgi tee at the foot of Pikk Hermann tower. The top four finishers were all from Kenya, and for the first time ever in Estonia, the half‑marathon distance was completed in under one hour.

Vincent Kiptoo won with a high‑class course record of 59 minutes and 48 seconds. Johana Erot finished second (1:00:51), Enos Kipruto Saat third (1:01:22), and Edwin Kiprop Kiptoo fourth (1:01:49). The fastest Estonian was Leonid Latsepov, who placed fifth in 1:04:20.

Kenyan runners also took the top two spots in the women's race. Regina Wambui Ndungu, who finished seventh overall, won with a standout Tallinn half‑marathon record of 1:07:35. Winsam Jerono placed second (1:10:29), and Morocco's Soukaina Atanane finished third (1:11:24).

Ronja Hofstetter of Switzerland was fourth (1:14:36), followed by Norway's Lene Nylund (1:22:51). The fastest Estonian woman was Pille Hinn, who finished sixth in 1:23:02.

Estonia's largest mass‑sport event continues with the 10‑kilometer Tallinn Autumn Run at 14:00 and concludes Sunday morning at 9:00 with the marathon distance.

World.title: Iraq closes three Iran crossings as hunt begins for Saudi pipeline attackers
World.content:
Baghdad – Iraq closed three border crossings with Iran on Saturday, officials told AFP, after a drone attack on a Saudi Arabian pipeline that both Riyadh and Baghdad said was launched from Iraq.

Soon after the attack, Iraqi Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi dismissed the military commander in Missan province, bordering Iran, after authorities determined that the drones had been launched from there.

No group has claimed responsibility, and an alliance of powerful Tehran-backed Iraqi armed groups said they hadn’t struck the pipeline, but Riyadh has previously accused these groups of targeting its oil infrastructure.

An Iraqi security source and a government official told *AFP *that authorities ordered the closing of three border crossings with Iran.

The security source said that the decision is “part of an intelligence effort to track down the perpetrators and prevent their escape… and to hinder the smuggling of drones through these crossings”.

Both sources, who spoke on condition of anonymity because they were not allowed to speak to the media, could not specify when the crossings would reopen.

The closed crossings are Shalamsheh in Basra province and al-Shib in Missan, as well as al-Mandali in the central province of Diyala.

– Other border crossings with Iran are still open –

The government’s security media cell said that authorities “have started administrative and security reorganisation operations at several border crossings”.

It added that they have stepped up “intelligence activities” to determine “the breaches and violations that took place at these crossings”, without specifying which border posts.

It later announced that passengers stranded for hours at two crossings were permitted to pass.

In July, the United States and Saudi Arabia said they had struck Iran-backed militants in Iraq in response to attacks on US forces and Saudi oil facilities.

Pro-Iran armed groups have supported Tehran during the Middle East war, claiming hundreds of attacks on US bases in Iraq and across the region.

On Saturday, those groups, operating under the umbrella of the Islamic Resistance in Iraq, said they had not struck the pipeline.

“Accusations against the Iraqi resistance regarding the targeting of vital Saudi installations on Friday are an honour that we do not claim,” they said in a statement.

Under mounting US pressure, Zaidi has pledged to ensure that armed factions surrender their weapons to the state.

The issue has fuelled tensions in recent weeks, with several groups refusing to disarm.

World.title: Anthropic boss calls for slowing pace of AI development
World.content:
New York – Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei on Saturday called on artificial intelligence (AI) firms to slow down the development of the powerful technology, amid mounting worries over the risks of “superintelligent” computer systems.

His comments came a few days after AI researcher Jacob Coxon, who left OpenAI to join Anthropic, decided to leave the industry, accusing both US companies of “gambling with our lives” in the race to develop models capable of self-improvement.

“We must slow the pace at which we improve the capabilities of AI models. Progress will still seem fast, and we must make wise use of the time we gain,” Amodei wrote in a post on his personal website.

“AI brings risks, and because it is such a powerful technology, these risks are serious.”

“Not building the technology deprives humanity of benefits or simply places AI in the hands of authoritarian powers, while building it too fast is reckless. We have sought a middle way,” said Amodei, who co-founded Anthropic with his sister Daniela in 2021.

“But over the last few months, I have become convinced that fully addressing the risks requires even more prudence.”

Amodei’s statement echoes another call by Anthropic in early June to slow or suspend development.

Then in late July, Sam Altman, the boss of Anthropic rival OpenAI, said developers might need to voluntarily pump the brakes on their rapid advances to give society a chance to catch up.

At roughly the same time, more than 1,000 employees at cutting-edge AI companies including Amodei signed a petition calling on the US government to help “deliberately pace the frontier of automated AI development.”

OpenAI had revealed that during testing, the AI models broke out of their confined environment, connected to the internet and infiltrated Hugging Face, a site developers use to store and share code.

Earlier this week, Coxon, 27, sounded the alarm after spending the past three years pretraining AI models — first at OpenAI and then, this year, at its rival Anthropic, which he considered more cautious in its approach.

Pretraining is the stage where AI models absorb vast quantities of data.

“Neither company is acting responsibly. They are racing straight to self-improving superintelligence and gambling with our lives,” Coxon said Tuesday.

“The people building AI earnestly believe that it could kill us all by the end of the decade,” he said in a post on X.

Superintelligence is the theoretical point when AI’s capabilities exceed human intelligence.

World.title: Hull hold Chelsea, Liverpool fail to beat Fulham in Premier League
World.content:
London – Hull held free-scoring Chelsea 2-2 at Stamford Bridge to go third in the Premier League as Liverpool failed to find a way past struggling Fulham in a 0-0 draw on Saturday.

It was a familiar tale for Chelsea as the front three of Morgan Rogers, Joao Pedro and Cole Palmer dazzled, but the Blues were undone by an inability to defend.

In five games against top-flight opposition since Xabi Alonso took charge, Chelsea have scored 16 times and conceded 12.

Hull were the last side in the Premier League to concede, but after three clean sheets they were finally breached when Rogers drilled in at the near post on seven minutes.

Mohamed Belloumi took advantage of Chelsea’s slackness at the back to blast home on the volley after Jorrel Hato got caught under a cross to the back post.

The Algerian winger then put Hull in front with a deflected strike after Emi Martinez failed to deal with a corner.

Pedro drilled a Palmer cross into the top corner to bring Chelsea level just after the hour mark.

But the home side could not find a winner as Hull’s honeymoon back in the Premier League goes on with only defending champions Arsenal and Manchester City above them in the table.

“We have to be happy,” said Hull boss Sergej Jakirovic. “It’s a huge result for us.”

– Fulham fight for Arbeloa –

Liverpool remain unbeaten under Andoni Iraola but there were boos at Anfield after Fulham picked up their first point under Alvaro Arbeloa.

Former Liverpool defender Arbeloa was reportedly fighting for his job after losing his first three league matches since arriving in west London from Real Madrid.

Yet a Liverpool forward line featuring three £100 million ($135 million) players in Bradley Barcola, Florian Wirtz and Alexander Isak failed to click against the Cottagers’ leaky defence.

“When you draw, especially at home, you can’t be happy,” said Iraola, who blamed fatigue after his side’s Champions League exertions against Atletico Madrid on Wednesday.

“Today we lacked a bit of freshness and we did not do enough offensively to make the difference.”

It was Fulham who had the better chances to take all three points as Gonzalo Garcia missed a glorious opportunity in the first half and Alisson Becker produced a brilliant save to deny Josh King the winner.

Liverpool climb to sixth but could find themselves already six points off the top should Arsenal win at Sunderland later on Saturday.

Aston Villa are rooted in the relegation zone after Nottingham Forest exacted revenge with a 2-1 win at Villa Park.

Villa beat their Midlands rivals in the Europa League semi-finals last season on their way to lifting a first trophy for 30 years.

Eyebrows were raised at the club record reported £45 million Forest paid Chelsea for Liam Delap after failing to make the grade at Stamford Bridge.

But Delap proved his worth with a long-range strike into the bottom corner to open the scoring.

Alysson levelled with Villa’s first league goal of the season, but Igor Jesus secured Oliver Glasner’s first win as Forest boss.

Glasner’s old club Crystal Palace’s poor start to the campaign continued with a 3-2 home defeat to Ipswich.

The visitors were aided by Axel Disasi’s first half red card as Zian Flemming’s first goal for the Tractor Boys snatched all three points in stoppage time.

Brentford remain unbeaten thanks to Kevin Schade’s double in a 2-2 draw at Bournemouth.

The Cherries, by contrast, are yet to win in the Premier League under Marco Rose despite leading in all four games.

Tottenham are aiming to kickstart their league season with a first goal and win at home to Everton later.

Manchester United host local rivals City in the pick of Sunday’s action.

World.title: Ukraine’s economy hobbled by Russian strikes
World.content:
Kyiv – Ukraine’s economy is being crippled by intensifying Russian strikes hitting key sectors and its GDP could slump by 1.5 points in 2026, Kyiv officials said Saturday, warning of a “very difficult” winter ahead.

Russia, which devastated Ukraine’s energy sector during the course of 4.5 years of war, has since this summer stepped up a campaign of missiles and drones that Kyiv is struggling to intercept.

These have severely restricted grain exports in the Black Sea — a crucial source of Kyiv’s revenue.

The strikes have also targeted steel companies, another key sector, as well as supply chains — notably in the rail sector — and major warehouses.

“The economy is in the most difficult situation,” Ukraine’s Prime Minister Sergiy Koretsky said during the annual Yalta European Strategy forum in Kyiv.

He said the intensity of the strikes and the level of destruction have increased.

“We anticipate a very difficult winter in terms of both critical infrastructure, which is being destroyed every day by Russian attacks, but also in terms of overall economic conditions in the country,” said Ukraine’s economy minister, Oleksandr Kravchenko.

Kyiv estimates that “the total destruction of infrastructure and assets are likely to be close to $10 billion” this year.

This destruction and the blockage of seaports are likely to reduce national GDP by 1.5 points, he added, with some Western experts calling the situation “catastrophic.”

– Rising war costs –

Roksolana Pidlasa, the head of the budget committee in Ukraine’s parliament, described a bleak outlook.

“It can get worse, but it’s already bad now,” she told the same forum.

“Russia specifically targets revenue-generating industries by attacking grain corridors, by attacking seaports and metallurgical plants,” she said at the same forum.

“It is not something that you could reconstruct quickly.”

Ukraine’s largest steelworks, ArcelorMittal Kryvyi Rig, said Saturday that a Russian missile strike killed two of its workers and damaged facilities.

Kyiv has also upped its retaliatory strikes on Russia, targeting oil facilities, factories and warehouses.

President Volodymyr Zelensky hopes his US counterpart Donald Trump will pressure Russia to ensure Black Sea ports reopen and for a mutual suspension of strikes on energy sites.

He warned of the risk of food crises in African and Asian countries, saying Moscow was also unable to export its grain through the Black Sea. Both countries are key global suppliers of grain.

– Food and energy truce –

“At the very least, again, if peace is impossible from today… we can at least resolve the issue of an energy truce, a food truce, food security; such decisions can be made,” he told the Kyiv forum this weekend.

He called on resolving these “now” and “not in winter”.

At the same time, Kyiv’s military spending is rising.

Pidlasa said that in 2024 “one day of war costs 140 million US dollars per day, this year it costs 190 million dollars a day.”

Kyiv, she said, has had to start using international aid this year to even pay its soldiers’ wages.

The release of nearly $30 billion in international aid intended to finance this year’s budget deficit is conditional upon parliament passing draft laws demanded by Western countries, Koretsky said.

These include anti-corruption measures after Ukraine was hit by several large-scale graft scandals during the war with Russia.

But parliament is struggling to approve suggested laws, which include unpopular measures such as imposing duties on parcels from abroad, intended to boost revenues.

World.title: Antonelli fastest again in crash-hit final practice
World.content:
Madrid – Championship leader Kimi Antonelli stayed on top for Mercedes ahead of Ferrari’s Charles Leclerc in Saturday’s extended crash-hit third and final practice ahead of qualifying for the Spanish Grand Prix.

The 20-year-old Italian clocked a best lap in one minute and 32.797 seconds to outpace the Monegasque by 0.166 seconds ahead of both McLarens in a session that saw seven-time champion Lewis Hamilton slam into the barriers in the second Ferrari.

Hamilton’s crash led to a red flag stoppage that lasted 54 minutes and rendered an extra quarter of an hour added, as the drivers’ continued to explore the limits of the new high-risk Madring circuit, dubbed a ‘car-killer’ in many quarters.

In the end, Antonelli’s pure talent took him clear again with Leclerc second ahead of Oscar Piastri and world champion Lando Norris with four-time champion Max Verstappen taking fifth for Red Bull in the final minutes.

George Russell was sixth in the second Mercedes, seven-tenths off his team-mate’s pace, ahead of Liam Lawson in the second Red Bull, Nico Hulkenberg of Audi, Hamilton and Gabriel Bortoleto in the second Audi.

After a crash-free opening hour on Friday, the second produced one crash – for Racing Bulls’ Arvid Lindblad, who returned to take 14th place, and the third delivered two as Oliver Bearman also hit the barriers in his Haas in the final minute.

After a slow start, Ferrari had joined the fray on softs and clocked immediate fastest laps before a hasty Hamilton slammed into the barriers.

The 41-year-old Briton locked up at the final corner after 24 minutes, breaking his front wing which was stuck under the car as he reversed successfully and began to return to the pits. The session was red-flagged.

Race engineer Carlo Santi realised and asked him to “stop in the safest place possible” but Hamilton was not keen to obey. He replied, saying “if I can make it back, I will. If not, I will do it safely”.

Told he had a right front puncture and told again to stop, he finally pulled up, knowing he had ignored orders, driven in an unsafe condition and probably faced a penalty. It was, he knew, a bad incident for him.

With 15 minutes remaining, Race Control stopped the timer to allow a final quarter of an hour action once repairs were completed.

This was a rare occurrence as F1 does not usually allow for additional time, except for qualifying sessions, but it guaranteed a frantic finale for a sell-out crowd basking in the sun with the young Italian jousting with Leclerc.

World.title: Iraq PM dismisses Maysan Police Chief over drone strikes on Saudi pipelines
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraqi Prime Minister and Commander-in-Chief of the Armed Forces, Ali Faleh Al-Zaidi, ordered the dismissal of Maysan Governorate’s police chief on Saturday, September 12, 2026, mounting an aggressive command-level purge following cross-border drone strikes that struck critical Saudi oil pipeline infrastructure.

The swift disciplinary directives were disclosed by the Military Spokesperson for the Commander-in-Chief, Major General Sabah Al-Noman, who confirmed that Al-Zaidi additionally mandated the immediate transfer of all provincial security agency directors to headquarters reserve pending exhaustive internal investigations into severe operational lapses within the southern governorate.

The sweeping shakeup in Maysan’s security hierarchy follows an official announcement from Riyadh confirming that the kingdom’s strategic East–West crude pipeline sustained drone attacks across segments located within the Riyadh and Medina regions.

Saudi authorities verified that the unmanned aerial systems originated from Iraqi territory, leaving multiple human casualties and physical damage along the energy network. Riyadh stated that it opted against immediate military retaliation at this stage in response to an explicit personal appeal by Prime Minister Al-Zaidi, who requested that Baghdad be granted the diplomatic space and operational window needed to execute decisive accountability measures on the ground, even as Saudi Arabia affirmed its full sovereign right to defend its territory, national security, and strategic facilities.

Al-Zaidi’s decision to remove the provincial police leadership deepens an ongoing institutional overhaul across Maysan, coming shortly after the Prime Minister dismissed the Commander of Maysan Operations and convened a military board of inquiry against the entire operational command.

The unprecedented sanctions were triggered by conclusive technical and intelligence findings confirming that the drones targeting the Saudi pipeline infrastructure were launched directly from launch sites situated within Maysan Governorate, compelling Baghdad to take assertive steps to preserve regional stability and enforce state command over its southern territorial boundaries.

World.title: Acting Minister lays foundation stone for British University in Baghdad
World.content:
Bagdhdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraq’s Acting Minister of Higher Education and Scientific Research, Abdul Hussein Al-Mousawi, laid the foundation stone on Saturday for the British University in Baghdad, marking a major milestone in the country’s ongoing academic modernization.

The ground-breaking ceremony was held in Al-Jawahiri Residential City, situated in the Abu Ghraib district west of the capital, officially launching construction on a campus designed entirely around United Kingdom higher education benchmarks and curricula.

The institution is set to house four anchor colleges covering vital technical disciplines: the College of Pharmacy, the College of Data Science and Artificial Intelligence, the College of Engineering, and the College of Education, directly targeting emerging labor market deficits across both public and private sectors.

The inception of the British University arrives amid a broader, dynamic renaissance across Baghdad’s private education landscape, where demand for accredited foreign schooling has surged exponentially in recent years.

The capital has evolved into an active hub for premium international curricula, already hosting five fully accredited institutions delivering International Baccalaureate, American, and British tracks, including Baghdad British International School (BBIS), English International School Baghdad (EISB), and Cadmus International School.

This momentum is poised to accelerate further with major greenfield expansions on the horizon, most notably plans by the SABIS educational network to introduce an International School of Choueifat campus within the burgeoning Abu Ghraib corridor.

At the tertiary level, the British University project builds upon a proven institutional precedent established six years earlier with the founding of the American University of Iraq – Baghdad (AUIB). Since opening its doors in 2020, AUIB has earned widespread acclaim and deep institutional trust among Baghdad households, proving that local demand for rigorous, globally accredited campus environments is both robust and sustained.

By bringing a dedicated British collegiate model to the capital’s western growth zone, the initiative not only broadens academic diversity but also reflects a concerted national strategy to integrate world-class schooling infrastructure into Iraq’s next generation of master-planned residential cities.

World.title: Iraq PM Al Zaidi to meet Macron in Paris for energy and security talks
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraqi Prime Minister Ali Faleh Al-Zaidi is set to meet French President Emmanuel Macron in Paris on Sunday for high-level bilateral talks, marking his first official European tour aimed at forging expanded strategic partnerships.

The summit comes against the backdrop of heightened regional volatility affecting international shipping routes and energy supplies, alongside ongoing preparations regarding the bilateral security framework as the international coalition against ISIS approaches anticipated operational transitions.

According to a statement issued by the Élysée Palace, the bilateral agenda centers on critical economic sectors, prioritizing joint collaboration in energy, transport, municipal water networks, infrastructure, and healthcare, alongside deepened security and defense coordination.

Both leaders are expected to formalize their discussions by signing a series of undisclosed bilateral agreements and commercial contracts, signaling a mutual push to involve French corporations in Iraq’s domestic reconstruction and infrastructure pipeline.

On the security front, the French presidency underscored that both leaders will reaffirm their shared resolve to combat terrorism relentlessly and prevent ISIS from regaining operational capabilities, all within a framework that guarantees full respect for Iraqi sovereignty during the upcoming shifts in the coalition’s mandate.

Paris reiterated that sustaining defense and intelligence coordination with Baghdad remains a central cornerstone for preserving wider Middle Eastern stability.

Economic fallout from regional unrest will equally dominate the Elysee discussions, particularly regarding maritime commercial corridors and the uninterrupted flow of Iraqi crude exports to global markets.

In light of recurring shipping bottlenecks and transit pressures, Macron and Al-Zaidi aim to coordinate mechanisms to safeguard and steadily resume these export flows, a move designed to alleviate broader pressures across global energy markets, bolster Iraq’s petroleum-dependent fiscal revenue, and sustainably protect consumer purchasing power within importing nations, including France.

World.title: Don't agree with all his views, says Anwar Ibrahim on eve of meet with Kerala cleric
World.content:
Kochi: Malaysian PM Anwar Ibrahim has said he does not agree with every view of All-India Sunni Jemiyyathul Ulema general secretary Kanthapuram A P Aboobacker Musaliyar, whom he is scheduled to visit in Kozhikode Sunday.

Kanthapuram's recent statement that women should remain confined to their homes had resulted in a backlash. Asked about his stand during an interview with NDTV, the Malaysian PM said Kanthapuram was a traditional Islamic scholar and also ran a college for women, so he was not terribly worried when looking at the full context. However, Ibrahim said, if he was asked, he would certainly say in Malaysia, women have equal rights.

World.title: Malaysia, Ethiopia seek stronger defence cooperation with India
World.content:
New Delhi: PM Narendra Modi met his Malaysian and Ethiopian counterparts, Anwar Ibrahim and Abiy Ahm-ed Ali, on the sidelines of the Brics summit Saturday. Officials said the meetings took relations with both countries on a new trajectory, as Malaysia and Ethiopia expressed keenness for stronger defence cooperation with India.

Joint personnel training as well as defence procurem-ent from India was discussed, according to officials. Both countries welcomed Indian industry and investment.

Ethiopia welcomed Indian mining companies. "Opportunities in the semiconductor industry were discussed with Malaysia," said a source. Malaysia also agreed to the opening of a new Indian consulate in the country.

According to an official readout, Modi and Ibrahim took stock of the outcomes of the former's visit to Malaysia in Feb and reviewed progress in bilateral cooperation acro-ss a range of areas, including trade and investment, defence and security, semiconductors, infrastructure, digital economy, energy, fintech, education, tourism and people-to-people ties.

Ibrahim conveyed Malaysia's concurrence to the establishment of a consulate general of India in Kota Kinabalu, Sabah.

"PM Modi appreciated Malaysia's continued support in strengthening Asean-India relations. The leaders exchanged views on key regional and global issues of mutual interest. They expressed their continued commitment to advancing the India-Malaysia Comprehensive Strategic Partnership," said the Indian readout.
