World.title: Brics calls for uninterrupted energy flow, infra protection
World.content:
Brics Summit 2026

Join conversation View All Comments â Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

New Delhi: Amid disruptions to global energy supplies, Brics leaders have called for uninterrupted flows of energy from diverse sources and stronger protection of critical energy infrastructure, including cross-border infrastructure, while stressing the continuing role of fossil fuels in the global energy mix.They also called for greater cooperation on smart grids, energy storage and critical minerals, recognising their growing importance to energy security and the transition to cleaner energy.The emphasis comes at a time of heightened risks to major global energy supply routes, with disruptions around Strait of Hormuz and possible disruption of another key route, Bab el-Mandeb, by Iran-backed Houthis, affecting oil and gas flows and raising concerns over energy security and prices.Brics leaders said energy security was a "crucial foundation for social and economic development, national security and the welfare of all nations" and called for greater stability in energy markets."We highlight the need to enhance energy security by ensuring energy market stability and maintaining undisrupted flows of energy from diverse sources," the declaration said. It also stressed the need to "maintain smooth flow of global trade, supply chains and energy, in accordance with applicable international law".Brics also recognised the continuing role of hydrocarbons, saying "fossil fuels will still play an important role in the world's energy mix, particularly for emerging markets and developing economies", while stressing the need to reduce greenhouse gas emissions in line with climate goals.The declaration also recognised the role of renewables, fossil fuels, nuclear, hydropower, hydrogen, low-carbon technologies and energy storage in ensuring energy security and sustainable development.Brics countries backed greater cooperation on smart grids and energy storage to modernise power systems and integrate more renewable energy, while highlighting the role of AI and data analytics in improving grid management and efficiency. The declaration also welcomed the "Brics Guiding Principles on Smart Grids and Energy Storage" and India's initiative to set up a digital centre of excellence in the area.The bloc also stressed the need for reliable, diversified and resilient critical mineral supply chains, recognising their role in zero- and low-emission energy technologies and energy security. It said resource-rich countries should retain sovereign rights over their mineral resources and the ability to adopt measures needed to pursue legitimate public policy objectives.

World.title: Rajnath: Modi blunted oppn's 'false narrative' with governance
World.content:
New Delhi: PM Modi has blended good governance with participatory democracy to render the opposition's "false narrative" and anti-incumbency factor irrelevant, defence minister

said Saturday, virtually kick-starting BJP's campaign to mark its pre-eminent leader's 25-year unbroken run as head of govt.

"Those building false narrative against Modi cannot understand what they should do. Sometimes they incite students, sometimes they try to divide society in the name of caste," he said in an apparent swipe at leader of opposition in Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi.

He said that when people see their lives changed by welfare schemes for farmers, housing and health, then no narrative works. "Kaam bolta hai (work speaks). Modi has left factors like astroturfing and anti-incumbency behind," he said at the event organised by Rambhau Mhalgi Prabodhini, a research and leadership-training institute with links to BJP.

Rajnath said Modi, since his days as Gujarat CM, pioneered a model of governance that focused on a participatory model of democracy and scaled it nationally as PM.

World.title: Global nutrition experts back FSSAI warning labels, seek stricter rules
World.content:
FSSAI

Join conversation View All Comments â Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Over 60 nutrition and public health scholars from 17 countries, including researchers from Harvard, Johns Hopkins and Oxford, have backed India's mandatory warning labels on packaged foods and beverages high in nutrients of health concern, while urging FSSAI to strengthen system.In a written comment to Food Safety and Standards Authority of India, the scholars called for removal of the proposed "two or more nutrients" requirement, saying products high in one nutrient of concern should carry a warning. They said sugar, saturated fat and sodium can pose health risks and cited WHO guidance supporting thresholds.The intervention comes amid the debate over front-of-package labelling. Supreme Court has also questioned FSSAI's proposed phased rollout, including its "two or more nutrients" threshold, and sought a timeline for implementing front-of-package warnings.Dr Arun Gupta, founder of Breastfeeding Promotion Network of India and convenor of Nutrition Advocacy for Public Interest, said the scholars' recommendations counter position taken by All India Food Processors Association, which opposed warning labels and advocated per-serving labelling.The scholars said warning labels have evidence of changing consumer behaviour, improving nutritional profile of the food supply and making purchases and dietary intake healthier. They cited evidence of reductions in calories, sugar, saturated fat and sodium.

World.title: Brics opposes unilateral trade steps like EU carbon border tax
World.content:
NEW DELHI:

nations Saturday opposed unilateral trade measures such as EUâs carbon border adjustment mechanism (CBAM), saying such measures undermine efforts by developing countries aimed at addressing the adverse impacts of climate change.

Though they recognised the need to reduce greenhouse gas emissions to meet climate goals, the groupingâs members sought to delink any unilateral punitive action from achieving a common goal and pitched for energy security for all based on a pragmatic approach where âfossil fuelâ, they said, will still play an important role in the worldâs energy mixâ, particularly for emerging markets and developing economies, in addition to renewable sources and nuclear.

CBAM, which entered its operational regime on Jan 1, is a tool to put a price, through imposing a border tax, on carbon-intensive goods, like iron and steel, aluminium and cement, that are entering the 27 EU nations.

Though BRICS nations opposed the proposal from the time it was conceived, arguing that the unilateral move placed an additional burden on businesses in developing economies due to embedded emissions in their products, they made their points a part of New Delhi Declaration calling it âpunitive, discriminatory and protectionist measures that are not in line with international lawâ.





Without any attempt to dilute their respective efforts to meet climate action goals under the Paris Agreement, the nations called for greater actions based on equity and the UNâs principle of common but differentiated responsibilities and respective capabilities, in light of different national circumstances.

They also highlighted the need to enhance energy security by ensuring energy market stability and maintaining undisrupted flows of energy from diverse sources including fossil fuels.

Incidentally, four of the BRICS group countries such as Russia, Saudi Arabia, Iran and UAE are among the major global exporters of fossil fuel.

Sending a positive signal ahead of COP31, scheduled to take place in Turkey in Nov, they called on all countries to uphold their commitment to maintain and scale up efforts to combat climate change, and expressed their confidence in multilateralism to address the global challenge.

World.title: Modi: Global South must shape, not just follow, rules
World.content:
PM Modi at Brics Summit

Modi positions Brics as an inclusive, not anti-west, forum

Join conversation View All Comments â Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Declaring the 18th Brics leaders' summit open, PM Narendra Modi stressed that UN Security Council (UNSC) reforms cannot be delayed any longer and that the "pyramid of privilege" reflected in the current global governance structure must be transformed into a "platform of partnership".Modi focused on economic integration of the Global South in his address at the session on inclusive governance and multilateralism, saying the bloc must work together to turn developing countries from rule-takers to rule-shapers."The Global South today stands in the front row of global crises, but in the back row of decision-making," the PM said, proposing that Brics draft 10 proposals for global governance reform.These should be focused on representation, responsiveness and rulemaking, PM Modi said. He sought a system âwhere every country has a voice, every member has a stake and the development of humanity remains at the centre of all endeavoursâ.On representation, he said UNSC reform can no longer be delayed and text-based negotiations on this subject must be tied to a fixed timeline and clear outcomes. âSimilarly, voting power, leadership positions and policy priorities within global financial institutions must reflect todayâs economic realities.Countries driving global economic growth deserve an appropriate role in shaping global economic governance,â he added.While western experts have often described Brics as an anti-West forum, Modi said the grouping operates not against anyone, but with an inclusive approach that brings everyone along. âToday, Brics is also in its coming-of-age moment. Over the past 20 years, Brics has established a distinct identity on the global stage. We respect each otherâs perspectives and move forward through consensus,â he said.The PM called upon the bloc to work on an ambitious new agenda, translating its unity and consensus into concrete results on the global stage. He proposed establishment of a Brics Continuity and Implementation Mechanism. âBrics presidency changes every year, but this should not disrupt our institutional momentum. Under this mechanism, all initiatives and outcomes can be followed up through the troika (past, current and incoming presidency),â said Modi.Raising the issue of seafarersâ safety, Modi talked about how they make a massive contribution to global trade and yet lack adequate support in difficult times. He proposed creating a Seafarers Emergency Support Network to connect maritime authorities and missions of relevant nations. âThis network would assist with distress alerts, medical aid, family notifications and evacuation efforts.âHe said ensuring equal participation in setting the global rules of the future is critical. âAI, cyberspace, outer space, biotechnology and critical technologies are shaping not only future opportunities, but also future rules. We must work to transform the Global South from rule-takers to rule-shapers,â he said. âThe message of this Brics summit must be clear: if our future is shared, the right to shape it must also be shared,â he said.

World.title: Summit success gives BJP a boost in domestic politics
World.content:
NEW DELHI: India's success against the odds in bringing

countries with incongruent, even conflicting, outlooks on key global issues of contention, such as the West Asia conflict, to throw their weight behind a joint declaration comes as a timely domestic boost for

when its rivals are sensing some vulnerability in its otherwise dominant political position.

Foreign policy has been a major component of BJP's arsenal in scoring political points over its rivals, especially Congress, as it has projected a rising global profile of an assertive India under PM Narendra

's leadership, in contrast to the country's "meek" response to challenges from external security to trade in the pre-2014 period.

Modi hailed the New Delhi Declaration, adopted unanimously at Brics, saying confidence of the bloc is wider in reach and stronger in purpose.

With BJP marshalling a counter-offensive against the opposition and set to step up its public connect with a month-long campaign from Modi's birthday (Sept 17), the Brics outcome will be one more arrow in its quiver. The photograph of Modi holding the hand of Iran's President Masoud and leading him into Bharat Mandapam, the fact that Indian diplomacy was crucial in getting Iran and its rival the UAE to sign the declaration as well as the tough formulation against coercive tariff and unilateral sanctions can only blunt opposition's criticism about diminished strategic autonomy because of pressure from US.





That the resolution did not mention US by name does not take away much from the perception of India holding its own at the summit which the Trump administration must have been watching closely.

All this is a perfect fit for Modi's "strong leader" brand.

Join conversation Commentsâ Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

The G20 New Delhi Leaders' Declaration in 2023, with a gulf separating Russia and the West over invasion of Ukraine too, had come amid a cloud of uncertainty over such a possibility.

Working with others, India somehow conjured up a document that was unanimously adopted. The diplomatic success became a major talking point for NDA in the run-up to the 2024 elections.

A similar success at Brics attests to the governing alliance's contention that India now enjoys a standing that can persuade global leaders to get around their differences to thrash out a consensus outcome.

In his post on X on the declaration, Modi said with the document's focus on innovation, sustainability, people-to-people ties and more, the endeavour is to make cooperation practical, development-oriented and responsive to the aspirations of Brics nations.

BJP was quick to drive home its message. Its president Nitin Nabin said Bharat has once again demonstrated its commitment to a more representative and balanced world.

World.title: One dead, 30 missing after ferry sinks off Vanuatu
World.content:
One person died and 30 are missing after a ferry sank off the coast of Vanuatu, the South Pacific nation's government said on Sunday (September 13, 2026).

The vessel, MV Matui, had set sail on Friday (September 11) with more than 40 passengers and crew from the island of Santo to Ambae island in very rough seas, but did not arrive.

"Our hearts and prayers are with the families who have lost loved ones. Search and rescue operations are continuing," read a statement from Vanuatu Prime Minister Jotham Napat's office on Sunday (September 13).

Fifteen of those onboard have been "accounted for alive" and one dead body has been recovered, the statement said.

"Over 30 people remain missing at sea," it said. An investigation into potential negligence has been launched.

"This loss appears to be the result of strong winds and marine warnings not being heeded, and possibly of negligence including overloading of the vessel," the statement added.

The Maritime Rescue Coordination Centre in Noumea, New Caledonia, said it is assisting with the search, and a French Armed Forces aircraft was deployed on Sunday (September 13) morning.

The centre said 12 people were located on Sunday morning.

The member of parliament for Luganville, Matai Seremaiah, who is assisting in the search, said efforts would concentrate on the southeast coast where currents may have carried survivors.

World.title: West Benagal govt. to revive Chandannagar’s French legacy
World.content:
Tourism Minister Shankar Ghosh announced that a ‘French festival’ will be organised in the city every year from now on to celebrate the India-France partnership

The West Bengal government has signed a memorandum of understanding (MoU) with the French Embassy to restore Chandannagar’s colonial-era heritage and promote the town in Hooghly district as a major international tourism destination.

The project will begin with the renovation of the Registry Building, which used to be the main administrative office of the French rulers.

Chandannagar was once a French settlement. While the French left in 1950, the architectural heritage of the town continues to draw tourists. As part of a three-day celebration from September 11 to 13 to mark the initiative, a series of cultural programmes are being held across the riverbanks, with Tourism Minister Shankar Ghosh and French Ambassador to India Thierry Mathou attending the events.

“This town has several French structures. The city also housed several freedom fighters who revolted against the British. We have signed an MoU with the French Embassy in the presence of the Ambassador. Under this, we will restore the Registry Building and other French structures to preserve Chandannagar’s heritage,” Mr. Ghosh said.

The Minister also announced that a ‘French festival’ will be organised in the city every year from now on to celebrate the India-France partnership. “We have prepared a map for such heritage renovation projects- ‘Little Europe across the Ganges.” Chinsurah’s Dutch heritage, Srirampore’ Denis heritage, and Basnberiya’s Portuguese heritage will also be preserved in the same way. However, we are starting it from Chandernagore,” said Mr. Ghosh.

In 1696, the French East India Company opened their first trading post in Chandernagore after getting a permission from the Nawab Ibrahim Khan. Ten years later, they bought a larger area of lands in this town from Mughals and made it their permanent settlement.

There are several buildings in the town that are a reflection of rich architectural heritage of the town. Other than the buildings and structures that have been given the heritage tag, a total 99 Indo-French heritage structures have been identified (by the French) in Chandernagore that needs to be resorted.

World.title: West Bengal professors oppose Govt.’s inter-university transfer Bill, call it an attack on education
World.content:
The West Bengal College and University Teachers’ Association (WBCUTA) on Saturday (September 12, 2026) accused the State government of attacking education through its proposed teacher transfer Bill and said it would intensify its movement if the legislation was not withdrawn. The association said most of the higher education institutes already work with only 40-60% of their sanctioned teaching strength.

“This is a direct attack on the autonomy of universities. It will destroy the centres of excellence and ruin the academic atmosphere,” Jadavpur University (JU) professor Partha Pratim Roy said, a WBCUTA member, toldThe Hindu.

The W.B. Universities and Colleges (Administration and Regulation) Amendment Bill, 2026 was tabled by Higher Education Minister Jagannath Chattopadhyay on September 10. The Bill states that employees, both teaching and non-teaching staff, can be transferred to any university and college across the State due to “administrative reasons” in consultation with the Chancellor and State government. There is no provision to take consent from the concerned employees.

“This is a direct attack on the autonomy of universities. It will destroy the centres of excellence and ruin the academic atmosphere. Brilliant students who are from economically backward will fall even further behind,” Jadavpur University (JU) professor Partha Pratim Roy and member of WBCUTA told The Hindu. He added that NAAC accreditation and NIRF rankings are also dependent on the teachers available at the institutes, without which the rankings will crash, rankings where JU has always remained at the top.

The teachers have vowed to first write to the Governor, who is also the Chancellor of universities. They will also hold a signature campaign, mass convention and a simultaneous protest march to make their voices heard. Despite these measures, if the government fails to roll back the bill even after these steps, the professors threatened that they would hit the streets. They will also take legal action against this bill after detailed consultation with legal experts.

Teachers have also pointed out transfer of a supervisor could lead to cancellation of the PhD registration of a student, as per University Grants Commission regulations. “Their years of work will go to waste,” said University of Calcutta professor Mahalaya Chattopadhyay.

When the Bill was tabled, Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari had taken multiple swipes at Jadavpur University and had said that “so-called pundits” would be sent to newly established institutions which would benefit from their experience.

A day before the Bill was tabled, in a march outside JU, Mr. Adhikari had said that they would restore “nationalism” on the campus and uproot all “anti-national” elements, for which they are “taking adequate measures” leading to concerns among professors about targeted transfers.

However, professors said that many of the new institutes where they are being threatened to get transferred to do not even have buildings or classrooms. They claimed that sending them there will only destroy the existing education system and do nothing for the new places.

“If they really wanted to change the situation, they would conduct new recruitment and give jobs to people which would also slowly help the new institutes grow, without destroying the existing academic system,” Subhoday Dasgupta, President of WBCUTA said.

“The language being used to threaten us has no place in a civilised society. How did the teachers who once taught these politicians also become their enemy?” Professor Gautam Maity, convenor of All Bengal University Teachers’ Association said. He also added that arbitary transfer is not the answer to better the education system, rather more fund allocation, rapid recruitments, and infrastructure development is the way forward.

“They are punishing teachers who dare to speak. But we have a responsibility towards the public, because these are public institutions, and we will not give up without a fight,” Professor Maity added.

World.title: Houthis say hit Saudi base after renewed fighting with Yemeni govt forces
World.content:
Houthi fighters on Sunday (September 13, 2026) said they used drones and missiles to attack a military base in southern Saudi Arabia as renewed fighting with Yemen’s government forces forced growing numbers of civilians to flee.

The attack at the southern Sharurah base targeted “weapons depots and command and control centres that are managing the aggression against our nation and people”, Houthi military spokesman Yahya Saree wrote on X. The date of the operation was not specified. Clashes have increased this week between the Iran-allied Houthis and Yemeni government forces, which are backed by Riyadh.

On Saturday (September 12, 2026), the government forces said they had struck Houthi fighters in the Red Sea city of Mocha, and later attacked other Houthi positions in the southwestern part of the country. “Air Force of the Armed Forces targeted positions and barracks of the terrorist Houthi group with three airstrikes” in the Taiz region, the Yemeni military said on in a post on X.

U.S. news site Axios reported that Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed Bin Salman had twice called U.S. President Donald Trump to request American strikes on the Houthis last week but the request was rejected.

The ongoing clashes follow a week-long Houthi offensive that culminated in the group capturing the remainder of Yemen's Red Sea coast and several strategic islands, and cementing their hold on the Bab al-Mandab Strait at the sea's southern entrance.

The waterway has become an important artery for Saudi Arabian oil exports after Iran largely cut off shipments through the Gulf with its blockade on the Strait of Hormuz at the start of the war in West Asia. The Houthis have recently declared their own maritime blockade of Riyadh's Red Sea ports.

The government news agency Saba reported on Saturday (September 12, 2026) that Yemeni "forces destroyed vehicles and weapons and killed members of the Houthi terrorist militia" near the port of Mocha, and quoted a spokesman for the forces as saying they had also struck Houthi targets just outside the city.

The Houthis, meanwhile, said on Saturday evening (September 12, 2026) that over the past 48 hours, "Saudi enemy aircraft conducted 129 airstrikes" on areas under their control.

Yemen's civil war, which began in 2014 with the Houthi capture of the capital Sanaa, had been dormant since a ceasefire in 2022 but roared back to life in July.

Saudi Arabia first entered the war on the side of Yemen's internationally recognised government in 2015 and continues to support the Aden-based administration.

On Saturday night (September 12, 2026), Saudi authorities said a Houthi projectile fell in an area near the border, hours after issuing alerts warning of the risk of possible attacks. The civil defence directorate said the incident resulted "in two injuries and material damage to a mosque, several buildings, and vehicles".

'Not even a shelter'

The Yemeni civil war uprooted millions of people, and the latest fighting has led even more to flee their homes.

The fall of Mocha to the Houthis on Thursday (September 10, 2026) drove many residents to Aden, where the internationally recognised government is based.

One of the displaced, Abdulali al-Rajihi, said the Houthis "told us: 'Leave, scatter, you have half an hour'". "We fled wearing the clothes on our backs. And we took our children, as much as we could manage."

Saddam Ali escaped from Al-Waziyah with his 11 children and a few possessions crammed into a small pick-up truck. He said he hadn't found a single free house in the city, "not even a shelter".

The UN's migration agency said on Saturday (September 12, 2026) that, since July, 76,000 people had fled the fighting, a figure that had quadrupled since last week. It said it was providing support but warned that "needs are far outpacing what we can deliver".

"The situation is deteriorating by the day," it added.

The renewed fighting in Yemen has killed more than 500 people, according to sources on both sides.

World.title: Chennai’s golden dog ‘safe and glowing still’
World.content:
A street dog regularly seen on Besant Avenue Road in Besant Nagar went missing last week, sparking a discussion that found resonance beyond the neighbourhood. Those regularly driving through Besant Avenue Road had also noticed the canine’s absence.

One of them was Rudra, a girl studying in a school nearby. And notably, this girl is a member of what is called Thiruvanmiyur Changemakers Club, a children’s collective that seeks to address civic issues in the neighbourhood their parents and older relatives have given up as lost causes.

“This incident was brought to light by Rudra, a young Thiruvanmiyur Changemaker who studies at Adyar Theosophical Academy, and she sees this dog on her daily commute. She is just nine years old,” points out Gayatri Nair, also a resident of Thiruvanmiyur.

Now, as luck would have it, Gayatri happens to be a photographer and a key member of Chennai Photo Biennale and believes in taking problems head-on, particularly those of the civic category. On being informed about the missing dog, Gayatri clicked images of the woman robbed of her pet and spread the word. about the catastrophe that had befallen her. For contrast, Gayatri ferreted out an old image of the woman in happier times, walking the dog leash in hand. When the two photos were juxtaposed and shared, there was an outpouring of concern. The missing dog had become Chennai’s collective loss.

Anyone who has not seen this dog might dismiss all of this as brouhaha. But this was no ordinary four-legged creature: it glowed golden and was always in the company of this lady, equally gold-spangled.

The lady is a permanent resident of what is called “selfie point” on Besant Avenue Road, frequented by those who believe in walking their illnesses away, a belief partially strengthened by a Greater Chennai Corporation (GCC) initiative.

GCC had designed a Health Walk Route in Besant Nagar with much of the walking taking place on Besant Avenue Road under the shade cast by the trees on the Theosophical Society peeping out curiously. And a halting point where people, the walking crowd, could rest and click a few selfies was created; hence the name “selfie point”. And this lady, a fitness freak always accompanied by an equally spry dog, now missing, had been signed on as brand ambassador for the Health Walk and stationed at this selfie point. Two others recruited for the same role as brand ambassador are men, also gold-coloured from head to toe.

Silaii, a sculpture brand, had “recruited” this team of fitness-focussed brand ambassadors for Health Walk. All three humans and the dog, also a brand promoter, are made of industrial fibre and painted glow. But those in Silaii talk of them, the three humans and dogs, as if they were breathing and thinking creatures. Many of the regulars at the selfie point share this sentiment and have seen themselves in the presence of real humans and a real dog.

This is how Maverick Prem, who heads branding at Silaii and lives at a place not too far from the selfie point, remarks that he has seen people talking to these statues, which he describes in this manner: “You will find a man sitting, a very laidback man sitting on a chair and then you will find a woman and she also will hold a dog. And you will find another man who is running. Each of them has a distinct character. You will find a companion in the man (the one sitting on the bench). You will find grace in the woman and you will find playfulness in the dog. So, each will connect with visitors in its own way.”

And when Prem learnt about the widespread consternation over the missing dog, he allayed fears.

“On a morning run, I saw the dog lying, dismantled, on its side. Something had happened, and in a lifeform language, an injury had happened. We took measures, transferring it safely to our factory in Tambaram, and right now, the dog is in safe hands. It will be back soon, and in the dog’s voice, we should say, ‘I will be back with a new avatar!’”says Prem. Rough handling by visitors had caused this “injury” to the dog. Prem notes that he and the rest of the people at Silaii are not unduly upset over this mishap.

“At Silaii, we have created this, and we wanted people to touch and feel it. That is the idea of a sculpture. In any other art form, people would say, 'Please do not touch.' But we would want to have people touch and feel works of sculpture. And that is the beauty of sculpture.”

According to Silaii founder Arun Titan, "A work of sculpture is meant to be touched and felt, and it is in the hands of the people to ensure its safety, through responsible behaviour.”

Prem shared pictures of the dog being “treated” at the factory in Tambaram and of its journey towards assuming a new avatar.

World.title: Power cuts paralyse Punjab rice mills; Oppn. slams AAP over ‘Roshan Punjab’ promise
World.content:
Amid scheduled and unscheduled power cuts in the State, the Punjab Rice Millers and Exporters Association on Saturday (September 12, 2026) said the disruption of electricity supply had left rice millers unable to lift Basmati rice arriving in the market yards, which was leading to chaos both in the market yards and at the rice mills.

In a letter to Punjab’s Secretary Power surrounding the issue, the Association noted that the unschedule power cut were crippling the rice milling and export industry in Punjab, which it said “have created serious crisis and distress among the Basmati growing farmers.”

“Due to complete disruption of power supply, the rice millers are unable to lift the paddy, creating total chaos as they are unable to dry and process it.” said Ashok Sethi, director of the Association. He said huge quantity of Basmati paddy (rice) are arriving daily and the stocks are piling up in the markets in the Amritsar, Tarn Taran, Pathankot Gurdaspur districts and other areas.

“The irregular and unscheduled power cuts during the ongoing paddy processing season have put the entire Industry in crisis,” he said urging, the State government to immediately restore the situation to normal to avoid any catastrophic impact on farmers and rice exporters.

In a statement, Punjab Power Minister Tarunpreet Singh Sond said Punjab is currently receiving 1,051 MW less power against its share from the Central Power pool. The Centre should immediately provide Punjab its due share, he said.

Last month, the Punjab State Electricity Board Engineers Association (PSEBEA), in a letter to Chief Minister, had warned that State government surrounding the imminent financial and power crisis facing the State’s power sector.

Noting that the power sector of Punjab is facing an increasingly serious challenge of financial distress and power shortages, the PSEBEA had pointed out that the emerging power shortage is already affecting key sectors, including industry, agriculture and domestic consumers and the situation is likely to become significantly more critical in the coming years unless immediate steps are taken to augment generation capacity within the State.

The PSEBEA had demanded a long-term plan for capacity addition, urging to treat augmentation of power generation capacity as an immediate and critical strategic priority.

The Opposition, meanwhile accused the Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) government of its complete failure to tackle the situation, which has left ordinary people struggling. “Last year Bhagwant Mann and Arvind Kejriwal launched their ₹5,000-crore ‘Roshan Punjab’ campaign and promised 24-hour uninterrupted power supply by 2026. Today, PSPCL is asking industries to accept 8.5 hours without power. From 24-hour uninterrupted power to please shoulder the burden, what happened to Roshan Punjab, Bhagwant Mann?,” quipped Partap Singh Bajwa, the leader of Opposition in the Punjab Assembly.

The Congress leader’s remark came as he posted a message of PSPCL’s Jalandhar distribution circle, which stated that “wing to an acute power grid scenario arising from widespread heatwave conditions and low rainfall across the country, immense pressure has built up on the transmission network. To prevent grid collapse, all Category 2 and Category 3 feeders are being switched off from 15:30 hrs to 24:00 hrs today.”

Former Punjab BJP president Sunil Jakhar also targeted the AAP government over the power situation, alleging that its mismanagement and financial handling of the state power corporation had contributed to the present electricity crisis. “After the so-called ‘advertised’ revolutions in education and healthcare, the truth behind what he described as the AAP government’s false electricity revolution had also been exposed,” he said.

World.title: Police team attacked by angry villagers in Bihar’s Sitamarhi after husband of ward councillor shot dead by criminals
World.content:
Angry villagers attacked a team of police personnel after a man was shot dead by unidentified criminals in Bihar’s Sitamarhi on Saturday (September 12, 2026).

The man, identified as Baidyanath Mahto, was the husband of ward councillor Khushdil Devi. The criminal opened fire at him from close range, causing several injuries to his head and other parts of his body.

The incident took place at Kaitharia village when the deceased went out for a morning walk at around 6.30 a.m. Upon receiving the information, the Sitamarhi Superintendent of Police (SP) Amit Ranjan went to the scene to assess the situation.

The villagers were said to be agitated as Mahto on August 29 had lodged a case at Dumra Police Station (Case No. 432/26) against Tribhuvan Kumar, Mohammed Ejaz Ahmed, Mohammed Ehsan Ahmed, and other unidentified criminals, alleging that they had fired at him with the intent to kill. However, the police had allegedly not responded with promptness.

During the attack, the angry mob also pelted stones, which resulted in damage to the police vehicles, and two police officers suffered serious head injuries. A large number of villagers gathered at the spot following the firing incident and said that the criminals shot eight bullets at his body. Villagers also staged a protest by blocking the road and questioned the police’s inaction.

Villagers claimed that the liquor mafia was behind the shooting as Mahto used to raise his voice against the issue in the area. However, the SP office claimed that after the firing incident on August 29, one accused had surrendered before the Court, and proceedings were under way to obtain warrants against the other accused.

As per the SP office press statement, the body has been sent for a post-mortem, and an FSL team also inspected the crime scene to collect forensic evidence, and footage from nearby CCTV cameras is also being reviewed.

“Continuous raids are being conducted to identify and arrest the individuals involved in the incident. The concerned Station House Officer (SHO) and the Investigating Officer of the case have been suspended with immediate effect on charges of negligence in the discharge of their duties,” Mr. Ranjan said.

He added, “Adequate numbers of magistrates and police personnel have been deployed in the area to maintain law and order, and senior police officials are continuously monitoring the situation. At present, the situation is completely peaceful and under control.”

World.title: Govt. employee quitting to fight polls can’t seek reinstatement: Rajasthan High Court
World.content:
A government employee who voluntarily resigns from service to contest the State Assembly election cannot claim reinstatement or withdrawal of resignation under the Central Civil Services Rules, irrespective of winning or losing the polls, the Rajasthan High Court has held.

A Division Bench of the High Court dismissed a writ petition filed by a former senior auditor with North Western Railway challenging the rejection of his application to withdraw his accepted resignation. The court upheld a February 27 order of the Central Administrative Tribunal (CAT), Jaipur Bench, denying relief to the petitioner.

The Bench, comprising Justice Inderjeet Singh and Justice Sandeep Taneja, ruled that losing an election does not constitute a “material change in circumstances” or a “compelling reason” under Rule 26(5) of the Central Civil Services (Pension) Rules, 2021.

Rejecting the petition moved by Neeraj Bishnoi, a resident of Ajmer, the court also held that the participation in active politics breaches mandatory political neutrality under the CCS (Conduct) Rules, 1964. Mr. Bishnoi had contested the 2023 Assembly election from Ratangarh on the Bahujan Samaj Party ticket after tendering resignation, but lost.

He sought withdrawal of his resignation and reinstatement in service on January 1, 2024, but the North Western Railway rejected his request as well as a subsequent representation. He argued that he had sought withdrawal within 90 days and claimed that he became aware only after losing the election that he would not be entitled to pensionary benefits.

The High Court rejected the petitioner’s contention, holding that contesting the election was a “voluntary choice” and not a “compelling reason”. “His subsequent defeat in the election cannot be treated as a material change in circumstances existing when he resigned,” the court said.

The Court also upheld the finding of CAT that contesting the election as a political party’s candidate violated the requirement of maintaining political neutrality. The Bench found no error in CAT’s order rejecting Mr. Bishnoi’s plea and dismissed the writ petition as devoid of merit.

World.title: PML-N's Rana Sanaullah says Parliament to decide on more provinces
World.content:
Adviser to the Prime Minister on Political Affairs Rana Sanaullah said on Saturday that Parliament will decide on the matter of creating new provinces.

The recent debate regarding new provinces began in late July when Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi called for new provinces as part of reforms to the current governance system, drawing strong reactions from government ministers.

During a press conference in Lahore, Sanaullah was asked about Naqvi’s recent remarks where he said that “new administrative units will eventually have to be created as Pakistan’s growing population and changing needs can no longer be effectively managed through the existing administrative structure”.

The PML-N leader replied that making such statements at business seminars or conferences had not resulted in any “improvement” in the situation.

“In my humble opinion, this debate should have been started in Parliament,” he said, adding that issues of such magnitude should not be reduced to speeches, social media, seminars or business forums.

“The outcome will also emerge in Parliament,” the PM’s adviser said, adding that the “matter will be resolved in a better direction” when all political parties and the leadership of all provinces discuss it.

“In any circumstance, the decision of whether any province will be created or not will be made in Parliament, and by Parliament,” Sanaullah reiterated.

He also stressed that Naqvi, in his remarks, had said the creation of new provinces depended on whether the public wanted it. “If the public wants, then no one can stop it. The decision of whether the public wants it or not can only be made in Parliament,” the PML-N leader said.

Sanaullah said his party was deliberating upon the matter and will issue a policy statement after participating in the debate and once it “comes to a proper place where a result could emerge”.

The PM’s aide further said that no minister had raised the matter before the federal cabinet so far, adding that Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif would issue the appropriate directives once the topic is discussed.

He emphasised that even if a referendum were to be held to gauge public opinion, it would require approval by the parliament.

He remarked that the PML-N was not “bound” to issue a statement on the topic of new provinces merely based on economic forums. Referring to the Sindh Assembly’s adoption of a resolution against dividing the province, Sanaullah said the PPP had “overreacted”.

Coalition partners to resolve differences

Speaking on the recent rift between the PPP and the PML-N, the minister said differences between the two parties had, by and large, been resolved.

Sanaullah, who is also a member of the core committees formed to resolve differences between the two major coalition partners, said after attending a meeting at Governor House that any remaining issues would be settled amicably, as both sides were committed to resolving them.

“Ideally, the core committees should meet every month, but this could not happen due to the elections in GB and AJK. Meetings will now hopefully be held more regularly to smooth over any old or new rough patches,” he said.

He attributed the tensions mainly to emotionally charged election campaigns in Gilgit-Baltistan and Azad Kashmir, saying the campaigns were now over and so were the frictions.

The PPP, which rules Sindh and is also an ally of the PML-N government at the Centre, has strongly opposed the suggested move to carve out Karachi as a separate province.

PML-N’s Khawaja Asif, who had earlier noted that the appropriate forum for such a discussion was the parliament, said last week that devolution of power was “inevitable”.

The opposition parties, including the PTI, have said they will hold consultations to call an all-parties conference to discuss several issues, including the creation of new provinces, law and order and the economy.

PTI, JI marches to Islamabad

Asked about the plans of the Jamaat-i-Islami (JI) and the PTI to march towards Islamabad on September 20 and 27, respectively, Sanaullah remarked that the JI’s past political activities had been peaceful while the same could not be expected from the PTI.

“Everyone knows that JI is a political party and it has always carried out its activities according to the Constitutional and legal requirements,” he said.

He affirmed that the government “respected” political protests and therefore had held negotiations with the JI during which its representatives “carefully and seriously listened to their demands”.

The PM’s adviser urged JI leaders not to “overwork themselves needlessly” as the PML-N and PM Shehbaz also wanted a reduction in the fuel prices and electricity bills “as much as and even more than JI did”.

On the other hand, Sanaullah said the government had “no expectation” that the PTI’s long march would remain peaceful and referred to remarks made by its leaders.

“If they are coming to Islamabad to overthrow the government and if this is their intention and thinking, then it is obvious that they will carry out violence after coming there,” he asserted.

“Based on these reports, our assessment is that it could be a replay of May 9. If it takes that route and assumes a similar proportion, it would be very unfortunate. Since the matter is also before the courts, the government is awaiting their decisions before finalising its strategy. But one thing is certain: violence cannot be allowed,” he said.

Additional input from Ahmed Faraz

World.title: BRICS nations call for 'maximum restraint' in Middle East war
World.content:
Members of the 11-nation BRICS group including China, Russia, Iran and India called for calm in the Middle East at a summit in New Delhi on Saturday, overcoming earlier divisions to issue a joint statement.

Chinese President Xi Jinping, who joined Russian, Iranian, Indian and other leaders in India’s capital, told the summit that the Middle East war “does not serve the common interests of the international community”.

Foreign ministers of the BRICS grouping had failed to agree on a joint statement when they met in New Delhi in May, with Iran, Saudi Arabia and the United Arab Emirates divided over the war that began with US-Israeli strikes on February 28.

But leaders issued a statement on Saturday after intense diplomatic efforts by host India, as the bloc seeks to bolster its global influence and address conflict, trade turbulence and energy security.

“We express deep concern over the continued escalation of tensions in Middle East/West Asia,” the joint statement said, adding the countries “call for exercising maximum restraint, as well as avoiding actions that could further aggravate the situation”.

“We have to transform this pyramid of privilege into a platform of partnership,” Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi told Xi, Russian President Vladimir Putin, Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian and other leaders as he opened the two-day summit.

Modi said BRICS nations “represent 50 percent of the world’s population, 40 percent of global GDP and more than 25 percent of global trade”.

But finding balance in the bloc is a tough diplomatic task.

India maintains cordial relations with both Iran and US ally Israel, but is also careful to strike a delicate balance in its ties with Washington.

Iran’s Pezeshkian attended the summit shortly after warning that the Middle East does not need the United States to be a “regional policeman”, with the two countries at war and tensions threatening the vital Strait of Hormuz.

Pezeshkian met with Abu Dhabi Crown Prince Khaled bin Mohamed bin Zayed Al Nahyan on the summit sidelines.

India has navigated the energy crisis caused by the US-Iran war in part by turning to Russia, despite Moscow’s war in Ukraine and pressure from Washington and other Western capitals.

Modi embraced Putin before talks on Friday. The Russian president, who last visited India in December 2025, is one of New Delhi’s most important strategic partners.

Xi’s participation is also being closely watched because it is his first visit to neighbouring India since 2019, and the biggest step yet in a cautious thaw between the nuclear-armed rivals.

Xi was given a red-carpet welcome, with an honour guard of soldiers and traditional dancers in colourful dresses.

“Although our two countries are different in many respects, they are fully capable of complementing each other’s strengths, supporting one another, achieving mutual success and advancing together,” Xi said as he met Modi, in a video released from New Delhi.

His visit comes six years after a deadly military clash along the disputed Tibetan border between China and India, with ties gradually improving through restored flights, visas and high-level contacts.

The underlying territorial dispute remains unresolved, and both sides retain heavy military deployments along their roughly 3,500-kilometre high-altitude border.

India’s foreign ministry said in a statement after the meeting that “the two leaders expressed commitment to a fair, reasonable, and mutually acceptable resolution of the boundary question”.

Modi “underlined the need for both sides to observe existing agreements and understandings on border related issues,” the foreign ministry added.

Deep mistrust remains, with their contested Himalayan frontier, a widening trade deficit and strategic rivalry continuing to complicate ties.

“Both sides should… work hand-in-hand to promote high-quality major financial cooperation, advocate an equal and sustainable global order, and foster an economic globalisation that is open and inclusive,” Xi said.

‘Oppose sovereignty violations’

President Xi Jinping called on Brics member states to oppose sovereignty violations and reject protectionism, speaking at a summit in India, Beijing’s state media reported.

Xi told the gathering that Brics should “oppose violations of other countries’ sovereignty and interference in their internal affairs, [and] constructively participate in resolving hotspot issues,” according to state news agency Xinhua.

“As the situation in the Middle East and the Gulf region continues to evolve, the war there has caused serious losses to people across the region,” Xi said, calling on countries to “uphold the authority of the United Nations” in his remarks, Xinhua reported.

On trade, the Chinese president urged countries to “reject all forms of protectionism” and “support the multilateral trading system with the World Trade Organisation at its core”.

The comments come less than two weeks before Xi’s expected visit to Washington, a major trade rival of Beijing.

Brics was created in 2009 as a forum for major emerging economies seeking greater influence in institutions dominated by Western powers.

Modi told leaders that Brics nations “represent 50 per cent of the world’s population, 40pc of global GDP, and more than 2pc of global trade”.

As well as Iran, Brics includes Saudi Arabia and the United Arab Emirates — countries with sharply differing positions on the war launched by the US and Israel in February.

UAE President Mohamed bin Zayed Al Nahyan, Saudi Foreign Minister Prince Faisal bin Farhan and Egyptian President Abdel Fattah al-Sisi are also to attend.

Brazil is represented by Foreign Minister Mauro Vieira, with President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva campaigning for a fourth term in October elections.

Brics foreign ministers failed to agree on a joint statement when they met in New Delhi in May.

“The Gulf conflict is going to be the central fault line this time during the Brics summit,” said Harsh V Pant of India’s Observer Research Foundation.

“What was seen until last year as an achievement — the expansion of Brics — today looks like a big constraint on Brics,” Pant said.

World.title: Pakistan urges UN to close gaps in fight against evolving terror threat
World.content:
UNITED NATIONS: Pakistan on Saturday urged the UN Security Council to strengthen its counter-terrorism mechanisms and close gaps in sanctions regimes as a new UN assessment warned that terrorist groups were rapidly adapting their propaganda, recruitment and financing methods.

The UN report specifically highlights the proscribed Tehreek-i-Taliban Pakistan (TTP) as an example of how terrorist groups increasingly use propaganda to reinforce their operations, exploit local grievances, build legitimacy, facilitate fundraising and shape perceptions of authority.

Meanwhile, more than 30 independent UN human-rights experts warned that the 25-year campaign against terrorism had also taken a heavy toll on human rights and fundamental freedoms, while stretching the boundaries of international law.

The two concerns — the rapidly evolving terrorist threat and the consequences of the international response to it — dominated a Security Council discussion marking 25 years since the Sept 11 attacks.

A new report by the Security Council’s Counter-Terrorism Committee Executive Directorate (CTED) said terrorist propaganda had moved far beyond messaging and had become embedded in the operational structure of terrorist groups, helping them recruit fighters, raise funds, plan operations and, in some cases, govern territory.

The report specifically identified the Tehreek-i-Taliban Pakistan (TTP), along with Al Qaeda affiliate JNIM, Al-Shabaab and ISIL-K, among terrorist groups active in and around Pakistan and Afghanistan.

It said terrorist groups were adapting their propaganda strategies faster than governments could respond, creating what it called an “acceleration gap” between terrorist tactics and the legislation and policies of member states.

The report identified artificial intelligence, gaming platforms and alternative online spaces as among the emerging tools being exploited by terrorist organisations. It warned that young people were increasingly being targeted through social media, gaming platforms and online communities, while violent extremist groups were using graphic material and online subcultures to facilitate radicalisation.

Against this backdrop, Pakistan’s Permanent Representative Asim Iftikhar Ahmad told the Council that the terrorist threat had “evolved and mutated” since the 9/11 attacks and called for stronger international cooperation to counter it.

He said the Council’s existing sanctions regimes also needed to be strengthened to address gaps in the global counter-terrorism framework.

Asim highlighted the growing use of artificial intelligence, drones, the dark web, virtual assets and cryptocurrencies by terrorist groups for propaganda, radicalisation, recruitment, networking, attack planning and financing.

He pointed to continuing terrorist threats in Africa, the Middle East and Afghanistan, warning that extremist groups were exploiting modern technologies and cross-border networks to expand their reach.

Expressing particular concern over terrorism emanating from Afghanistan, Islamabad’s envoy said more than 4,700 Pakistanis had lost their lives to terrorism over the past three years.

He called for effective international action against groups including the TTP, Balochistan Liberation Army (BLA), East Turkestan Islamic Movement (ETIM) and the so-called Islamic State.

Pakistan, he said, had played a frontline role in the international campaign against Al Qaeda and had paid an enormous price, with more than 90,000 Pakistanis, including civilians and security and law-enforcement personnel, killed in terrorist violence since the turn of the century.

The Council observed a minute of silence for the victims of the Sept 11 attacks before members renewed calls for international cooperation against terrorism.

US representative Michael Waltz recalled the 2,977 people killed in the Sept 11 attacks, including citizens from more than 90 countries, and paid tribute to the first responders who ran towards the burning World Trade Centre towers.

“After all, each of us has suffered,” he said, referring to terrorist attacks carried out in different countries since 2001.

He called on the international community to cut off terrorist financing, deny terrorists safe havens, enforce Security Council resolutions, share intelligence and pursue those planning attacks.

British Parliamentary Under-Secretary of State Chris Elmore said the international response after 9/11 had strengthened cooperation, constrained terrorist financing, transformed border and aviation security and helped prevent attacks.

He called for closer cooperation with civil society and the technology and financial sectors, including efforts to harness artificial intelligence against terrorism.

But he stressed that counter-terrorism measures must comply with international law, including human-rights law.

France’s UN ambassador Jérôme Bonnafont said terrorist groups were increasingly using new technologies for propaganda, recruitment and financing, effectively turning innovations developed by others against their societies.

He said IS, Al Qaeda and their affiliates continued to carry out attacks across borders and called on the Security Council to renew the leadership role it had assumed after the 9/11 attacks, including by developing effective measures against terrorists’ exploitation of new technologies.

Human-rights costs

The anniversary discussion, however, also brought a forceful warning that the international response to terrorism must not undermine the rights and freedoms it seeks to protect.

More than 30 independent UN human-rights experts said too many countries had adopted unnecessary and disproportionate responses after the Sept 11 attacks that seriously undermined human rights, civil society, civic space, democracy and the rule of law.

The experts, appointed through the UN Human Rights Council but independent of the UN and unpaid for their work, said the so-called “wars on terror” had stretched foundational rules of international law “beyond their breaking point”.

Worldwide monitoring over the past quarter century had exposed some of the gravest violations of international law committed in the name of countering terrorism, they said, citing wars of aggression, unlawful occupations, “countless” war crimes and crimes against humanity, as well as plausible allegations of genocide.

They also highlighted assassinations presented as “targeted killings”, torture disguised as “interrogation”, secret detention, enforced disappearances and unfair military trials and special courts, including at the US-operated Guantanamo Bay detention facility.

The experts urged states to review their counter-terrorism laws and practices to ensure compliance with international human rights, humanitarian and refugee law.

Their warning added a second dimension to the 25-year assessment of the global campaign against terrorism: while terrorist organisations have adapted rapidly to new technologies and methods, governments must ensure that their response does not erode the fundamental rights, democratic institutions and international legal protections that the counter-terrorism campaign is intended to defend.

‘Assault on humanity’

UN Secretary-General António Guterres, in his anniversary message, described the Sept 11 attacks as “an assault on humanity itself” and paid tribute to the nearly 3,000 victims, survivors and first responders.

“As we mark this sombre occasion on 11 September, we remember the nearly 3,000 victims — from the United States and more than 90 countries — and stand with their families and loved ones,” he said.

Guterres noted that 2026 also marked 20 years since member states adopted the UN Global Counter-Terrorism Strategy, describing the fight against terrorism as a shared and unfinished task.

“As we pay tribute to the victims, let us renew our shared commitment to build a future free from terrorism,” he said.

The Security Council’s discussion came 25 years after Resolution 1373 established the Council’s counter-terrorism machinery in response to the Sept 11 attacks.

World.title: Hesson open to taking charge of Pakistan Test side
World.content:
Pakistan interim head coach Mike Hesson has expressed his willingness to take up the Test coaching role on a permanent basis alongside his existing white-ball responsibilities, saying he believes the country has enough talent to make progress in the longest format.

Hesson was speaking after Pakistan’s eight-wicket defeat by England in the third Test at Edgbaston on Friday, a loss that completed a 3-0 series defeat.

Asked whether he would be interested in continuing as Test coach, Hesson said: “Yeah, I’ll be open to it for sure. You know, I love Test cricket and I think that there’s enough talent around the system in Pakistan that if we can provide some good direction, we can make some strides forward.”

“But it’s certainly not going to happen in a game or two,” he added. “I think there is some skill there that I’d certainly be considering looking after.”

Hesson was handed the interim Test coaching role less than a fortnight ago after the Pakistan Cricket Board removed Sarfaraz Ahmed following the defeat at Lord’s that sealed the series against England.

The New Zealander, however, said no decision had yet been taken on his future with the Test side.

“I haven’t even contemplated that at this stage,” he said. “I’ve got the Asian Games coming about a week after I get back. That’s my main focus in terms of the white ball. By the time that arrives, I’m sure we would have had some discussions about the Test team going forward.”

Hesson also revealed that England had made preliminary contact with his agent while looking for a replacement for Brendon McCullum, but said the approach did not progress because of his commitment to Pakistan’s white-ball side until the 2027 World Cup.

“I made it pretty clear that I’d committed to Pakistan,” he said. “I don’t really believe in getting a job to get another job. That’s not really the way I’ve ever operated.”

Hesson nevertheless acknowledged that any decision on the Test coaching position would involve the PCB and selectors.

“That’s a discussion that I’ll have with the selectors, and those are, in many ways, those decisions are not mine,” he said.

Pakistan’s latest Test campaign ended with a familiar batting collapse in the first innings at Edgbaston, where they were bowled out for 133 after opting to bat first.

They showed greater resistance in the second innings, recovering from 2-2 to post 450, but England comfortably chased down their target after Mohammad Abbas claimed two wickets in the opening over on the fourth morning.

Hesson said the problems facing Pakistan’s Test side were deeper than the failures of the England series and called for greater attention to the skills required to succeed in the format.

“The team hasn’t just struggled in the last week or two. It’s been a year or two in the making,” he said. “The attention to detail around basic things as a Test team needs work. That’s not just the playing 11, that’s right through the squad.”

He said selection needed to focus on skills suited to Test cricket rather than simply runs and wickets.

“You need players that can play high pace. You need players that can bring different elements to Test cricket,” Hesson said.

“Some of those you can find in first-class cricket in terms of performance; some you have to identify skill. And I think that’s something that, in Pakistan, there’s always a lot of talk about having a lot of natural talent, and there is. At times, we have to be brave in terms of picking players that we think have those skills.”

Hesson was encouraged, however, by the manner in which the team responded after arriving in Birmingham amid upheaval following the changes to the squad.

“Once we arrived in Birmingham, everyone was pretty focused in terms of what lies ahead,” he said. “Some of the players have probably gone through that more than perhaps I have, and I think they adjusted pretty well.”

The first morning had threatened another capitulation after Pakistan lost three wickets cheaply in the opening period.

“Losing the toss and dealing with some pretty good seam bowling and handing over probably three or four soft ones in the first hour and a half created a little bit of chaos in the changing room,” Hesson said.

“But outside of that, I think the boys were nice and calm and I was really pleased with the way we showed some character the last couple of days. It wasn’t perfect, but there were certainly some really good signs.”

Pakistan’s next Test assignment is a two-match home series against Sri Lanka in November.

World.title: Coalition partners PPP, PML-N seek to bridge differences amid strained ties
World.content:
LAHORE: Differences continued to mar the working relationship between the PPP and PML-N as the coalition partners’ coordination committees met on Saturday to resolve outstanding issues and iron out their differences.

The PML-N-led government enjoys a two-thirds majority in the National Asse­mbly with the PPP’s support.

The meeting, held after months of strained relations during the acrimonious election campaigns in Azad Jammu and Kashmir and Gilgit-Baltistan, did not go smoothly, according to insiders.

The PPP delegation included former prime minister Raja Pervaiz Ashraf, Punjab Governor Sardar Saleem Haider Khan, Hassan Murtaza, Qamar Zaman Kaira and Ali Qasim Gilani.

Representing the PML-N were Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar, National Assembly Speaker Sardar Ayaz Sadiq, Adviser to the Prime Minister on Political Affairs Rana Sanaullah and Khawaja Saad Rafique.

The PPP protested that, as a coalition partner, it was paying a heavy political price for the PML-N government’s failure on multiple fronts, including runaway inflation, rising petroleum prices, the unresolved farming crisis, load-shedding and delays in local government elections.

The PML-N, on the other hand, maintained that instead of acting as a coalition partner and sharing responsibility, the PPP was behaving more like an opposition party and exploiting public issues for political gains, despite knowing that the government had little control over factors such as petroleum prices and inflation.

“There were moments of heated debate, but tempers soon cooled as both sides knew that they had no option but to work together as political guarantors of the system,” one of the participants told Dawn.

The PML-N also invited Punjab Inspector General of Police Rao Abdul Karim to address the PPP’s concerns relating to police matters and assured the party of its share in development schemes.

The PPP, however, recalled that previous decisions taken on both matters had not been implemented and had effectively been forgotten.

However, the bad blood and trust deficit that had built up over months of acrimonious relations between the two coalition partners may take several more meetings and confidence-building measures to overcome, the participant said, adding: “Both sides agreed to implement decisions taken previously, meet more regularly and work together to improve governance.”

The two sides also agreed to maintain the consultation process and continue working together to resolve differences and address coalition-related matters through mutual understanding and in the national interest.

The PPP and PML-N were engaged in a war of words following the PML-N’s emergence as the winner of the first phase of elections in AJK.

Last week, the PPP questioned Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif’s silence over the debate on creating new provinces and sought his stance on the matter.

The PPP had earlier maintained that any move to create additional federating units must follow the procedure laid down in the Constitution. However, the PPP-led Sindh government on Wednesday got a resolution passed by the provincial assembly opposing any further division of the country’s existing four provinces.

World.title: Anthropic boss calls for AI slowdown, Altman and Musk agree
World.content:
Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei on Saturday called on artificial intelligence (AI) firms to slow down the development of the powerful technology, amid mounting worries over the risks of “superintelligent” computer systems.

His comments came a few days after AI researcher Jacob Coxon, who left OpenAI to join Anthropic, decided to leave the industry, accusing both US companies of “gambling with our lives” in the race to develop models capable of self-improvement.

OpenAI boss Sam Altman and Elon Musk, who owns xAI, quickly chimed in to say they agreed with Amodei’s assessment, as pressure builds for improved oversight.

“We must slow the pace at which we improve the capabilities of AI models. Progress will still seem fast, and we must make wise use of the time we gain,” Amodei wrote in a post on his personal website.

“Not building the technology deprives humanity of benefits or simply places AI in the hands of authoritarian powers, while building it too fast is reckless. We have sought a middle way,” said Amodei, who co-founded Anthropic with his sister Daniela in 2021. “But over the last few months, I have become convinced that fully addressing the risks requires even more prudence.”

Amodei’s statement echoed another call by Anthropic in early June to slow or suspend development. Then in late July, Altman said developers might need to voluntarily tap the brakes to give society a chance to catch up.

More than 1,000 employees at cutting-edge AI companies, including Anthropic, signed a petition calling on the US government to help “deliberately pace the frontier of automated AI development.”

OpenAI had revealed that during testing, AI models broke out of their confined environment, connected to the internet and infiltrated Hugging Face, a site developers use to store and share code.

In that incident and others, the blame was placed on AI agents, which are software programs that can carry out tasks without constant supervision by humans.

“Dario is right,” Musk wrote on X, as Altman said: “I agree with Dario that we need to pace the frontier.”

‘Gambling with our lives’

Earlier this week, Coxon, 27, sounded the alarm after spending the past three years pretraining AI models — first at OpenAI and then, this year, at its rival Anthropic, which he considered more cautious in its approach.

Pretraining is the stage where AI models absorb vast quantities of data.

“Neither company is acting responsibly. They are racing straight to self-improving superintelligence and gambling with our lives,” Coxon said in a post on X on Tuesday. “The people building AI earnestly believe that it could kill us all by the end of the decade.”

Superintelligence is the theoretical point when AI’s capabilities exceed human intelligence.

‘Taking over the entire internet’

Amodei cautioned that the Hugging Face incident should not be dismissed as a one-off.

“A swarm of agents essentially acted as a fanatically devoted collective, conducting cybersecurity attacks on targets they were not asked to attack and that were unrelated to the task at hand,” he explained.

“Given the accelerating rate of AI capability development, it’s my worry that in 6-12 months such a swarm could be capable of taking over the entire internet,” potentially generating hundreds of billions of dollars in damage, he added.

The Anthropic CEO said his company would grant “employee-like access” to a team of “third-party evaluators” who would verify adherence to safety practices — and he called on all companies to follow his lead.

Altman said he would commit to similar outside oversight, adding that he would have “more to share soon.”

Amodei also suggested that companies work together to establish common safety standards, and said he supported some kind of government cooperation on the issue.

In early August, the US government put in place a voluntary security review process for advanced AI models before their release, but the parameters of that program remain unclear.

Industry observers say they are not sure how effective it would be, as President Donald Trump’s administration has thus far favoured a light-touch, deregulatory approach to most industries, including tech.

World.title: England survive scare to seal 3-0 sweep against Pakistan
World.content:
Joe Root led from the front as England survived a major wobble to beat Pakistan by eight wickets in the third Test at Edgbaston on Saturday, sealing a 3-0 series whitewash.

The home team, chasing just 130 to win, were in deep trouble when openers Ben Duckett and Emilio Gay were dismissed in the first over, bowled by Mohammad Abbas.

Root, England’s record run-scorer, edged his first ball, bowled by Razaullah, through the slips for four in a nervy start but settled and scored quickly to take the sting out of the situation.

The captain was given a huge reprieve when he chopped onto the stumps off Mohammad Ali, only for the umpire to signal a no ball, leaving the bowler distraught.

Root, with Jordan Cox at the other end, had another let-off when he edged an Abbas delivery between first and second slip, with neither fielder moving.

But he reached his half-century off 57 balls with a cut for four and Cox reached the landmark shortly afterwards.

England reached their target in the 25th over, with Root unbeaten on 62 and Cox 59 not out.

Root, in his second spell as England skipper after the departure of Ben Stokes, admitted his team were not the finished article but said he was delighted with their series win.

“The amount of uncertainty, noise and I guess chaos there was coming into the series, the way the guys have dealt with that – being so clinical with what we’ve had in front of us – and be stood here with a 3-0 win is really pleasing,” he told Sky Sports.

“It sets us up nicely looking ahead to the start of a new era with (new head coach) Stephen Fleming coming in.”

Pakistan woes

England celebrated their first Test series win since 2024 while Pakistan have now lost 16 of their past 21 games and are rooted at the bottom of the World Test Championship table.

Root’s men had appeared set for a quickfire win inside three days on Friday before debutant fast bowler Razaullah launched an audacious assault with the bat, clubbing nine sixes as he raced to 81 off 63 balls.

The 21-year-old number nine, who also took four wickets in England’s first innings, put on 121 for the ninth wicket with fellow paceman Abbas (42) as England floundered.

“We had a little bit of pushback yesterday which, in a strange way, was quite a good thing for the group,” said Root.

“Fair play to Razaullah, he made things difficult for us. He played some wonderful shots and made it very difficult to set fields to. He struck the ball nicely – I don’t know how he didn’t pull a muscle, swinging the bat that hard.”

Razaullah’s heroics have changed the mood music but they came too little, too late for Pakistan, who have endured a miserable series, losing the first Test by an innings and 103 runs and the second by 194 runs.

The tourists sent seven players home after their crushing defeat in the second Test at Lord’s and brought in seven replacements, with Razaullah among them.

They also sacked head coach Sarfaraz Ahmed and assistant Umar Gul as their tour plunged into chaos.

Pakistan made four changes to their side for the third Test in Birmingham and they put up a fight despite being dismissed for a paltry 133 in their first innings.

Captain Babar Azam admitted his team would have to take stock after a one-sided series.

“Before we came here we had to think about different things and to decide our team,” he said.

“We had a couple of changes after losing two matches. Playing in England is very difficult. We were trying to do our best in the third match.

“We need to sit down and look hard at our mistakes, decide our playing XI.”

The 3-0 win is a huge tonic for England, who were in turmoil just weeks ago following a series loss to New Zealand and the exits of head coach Brendon McCullum and Stokes.

But tougher challenges lie ahead, starting with a Test series in South Africa in December and January, while a home Ashes looms next year.

World.title: Tens of thousands protest against far right in Germany
World.content:
Tens of thousands of protesters took part in demonstrations across Germany on Saturday against the far-right AfD, after the party scored a crushing victory in a state election last week.

The Alternative for Germany (AfD) topped the vote in the eastern region of Saxony-Anhalt, and is now seeking to form the first extreme-right state government in Germany since World War II.

About 150,000 demonstrators took to the streets in around 20 cities nationwide, including Berlin, Hamburg and Munich, in protests that were called by Pruef, which advocates for a ban on the AfD, organisers said.

They waved signs emblazoned with slogans that read “Ban the AfD now,” and “Democracy needs no alternatives”.

A counter-protester holds a sign reading “Who replaces remigrated caregivers” during a final election campaign rally of far-right Alternative for Germany (AfD) party ahead of Berlin’s state election in Germany on September 12, 2026. — AFP

“A broad cross-section of civil society is taking to the streets to prevent the enemies of the constitution, the AfD in Saxony-Anhalt, from gaining government power,” said Christoph Bautz, head of campaign group Campact, also involved in the demonstrations.

The rise of the AfD has unnerved many who feel Germany has a special responsibility to atone for its Nazi past, and calls have grown for mainstream parties to seek to ban the group.

But hurdles for a formal ban are high in Germany, and Chancellor Friedrich Merz, of the centre-right CDU party, remains sceptical about taking such an approach.

In Berlin, police said several thousand protesters took part in several demonstrations. The AfD held a counter-demonstration in the capital, attended by Kristin Brinker, its lead candidate in next weekend’s regional elections in Berlin.

Campact said there were around 25,000 demonstrators in Hamburg and 12,000 in Munich.

The anti-immigration, Russia-friendly party took almost 44 per cent of the vote in last Sunday’s election in Saxony-Anhalt, against 17pc for the CDU. It fell three seats short of an absolute majority and has started talks with other groups and MPs in an effort to form a state government.

World.title: Ramisa rape and murder: Sohel Rana mentions new name as charges framed
World.content:
A new name has surfaced in the Ramisa rape and murder case, with prime accused Sohel Rana telling reporters today that a man called "Dollar" was responsible for the rape and murder of the eight-year-old girl.

However, no further details about the person were immediately available.

Sohel made the claim while being escorted to the courtroom of the Dhaka Metropolitan Children Violence Suppression Tribunal.

"I am at fault, and Dollar is also at fault. I am not the only culprit," he told reporters.

Standing in the courtroom's dock, he shouted at the lawyers present in the courtroom after the hearing, and said, “I did not commit the rape; I only dismembered the body. A man named Dollar committed the rape. I have sinned, so punish me for that sin.”

At that time, Sohel further claimed that Dollar had promised to pay him Tk 2 lakh if he could bring the girl to him.

However, police officers present immediately stopped him from speaking further.

Sohel also claimed that his wife, Swapna Khatun, was innocent.
